zh: 7.1　摹仿与巫术
en: 7.1　Mimesis and Sorcery

zh: 我现在转向再现性艺术的人类学理论，即具有相关原型的索引的生产、流通与实际使用——这是几何纹样所缺乏的。大多数西方艺术属于这一类型，大多数艺术理论也以这样那样的方式谈论再现。我将尽可能避免讨论西方艺术，尽管这样做很诱人。相反，这部分论证围绕巫术与图像崇拜这两个经典“人类学”主题展开。
en: I now turn to the anthropological theory of representational art, that is to say, the production, circulation, and practical use of indexes that have relevant prototypes, something that geometric patterns lack. Most Western art is of this type, and most of art-theory is about representation, in one way or another. I shall try to avoid, as far as possible, discussing Western art, tempting though it is to do so. Instead, this part of the argument pivots around the classically ‘anthropological' themes of sorcery and image-worship.

zh: 重申一下，本书的基本论点是：艺术品、形象、圣像之类，在人类学理论的语境中必须被当作类似于人的存在来对待，即社会能动性的来源与目标。在这一语境中，偶像崇拜占据核心位置，因为没有任何地方比在崇拜和仪式中更明显地把图像当作人一样对待。本章中，我提出一个关于偶像崇拜的一般理论；我绝不认为这种实践比任何其他宗教仪轨更误入歧途；而且我希望，尽管我自己并不信教，我仍能对一般宗教保持同情的态度。自基督教与伊斯兰教崛起主宰世界以来，“偶像崇拜”一直名声不佳，两者都继承了《圣经》犹太教排斥圣像的传统。基督教背负着希腊—罗马遗产，不得不更积极地与事实上“异教”偶像崇拜的死灰复燃作斗争，并经历过灾难性的破坏圣像事件；伊斯兰教则更一贯地抵制指向形象的崇拜形式的诱惑。新教是过去几个世纪基督教中最有活力的分支，在偶像崇拜问题上几乎不比伊斯兰教更少清教色彩，而天主教徒的良心也常因此受到刺痛，以致今天的净结果是：“偶像崇拜”是一个贬义词，人类学家——尤其是声称能共情他人宗教情感的人类学家——不该使用它。但我宁愿用其真名称呼崇拜形象的实践，而不愿诉诸某种含糊或误导的迂回说法；我认为更好的做法是解释偶像崇拜，而不是给它重新命名——通过表明它并非源于愚蠢或迷信，而是源于同一种感同身受的能力，正是这种能力使我们能够把人类的、非人工制品的“他者”理解为一个共在的存在，赋有与我们相似的觉知、意图与激情。
en: The basic thesis of this work, to recapitulate, is that works of art, images, icons, and the like have to be treated, in the context of an anthropological theory, as person-like; that is, sources of, and targets for, social agency. In this context, image-worship has a central place, since nowhere are images more obviously treated as human persons than in the context of worship and ceremonies. In this chapter, I present a general theory of idolatry, a practice I by no means regard as more misguided than any other religious observance; and I am, I hope, capable of sustaining a sympathetic attitude towards religion in general, despite not being a religious person myself. ‘Idolatry' has had a bad press since the rise to world domination of Christianity and Islam, which have both inherited the anti-imagistic strain of biblical Judaism. Christianity, encumbered with its Graeco-Roman inheritance, has had to struggle more actively with recrudescences of de facto ‘pagan' idolatry, and has experienced cataclysmic episodes of iconoclasm; Islam has more consistently resisted the lure of image-directed forms of worship. Protestantism, the most dynamic branch of Christianity in the past few centuries, has hardly been less puritanical about idolatry than Islam, and the consciences of the Catholics have been often pricked on this account as well, so that the net result is today that 'idolatry' is a pejorative word, which anthropologists, especially ones who claim to empathize with the religious sentiments of others, are not supposed to use. But rather than resort to some vague or misleading circumlocution I prefer to call the practice of worshipping images by its true name, deeming it better to explain idolatry, rather than rechristen it by showing that it emanates, not from stupidity or superstition, but from the same fund of sympathy which allows us to understand the human, non-artefactual, ‘other' as a copresent being, endowed with awareness, intentions, and passions akin to our own.

zh: 即便承认偶像崇拜可以如此称呼，我仍需解释：为什么一本表面上谈“艺术”的书，必须把这么多页献给一个似乎属于宗教研究而非美学的主题。反对我反美学立场的人，会认为形象的“宗教功能”不相干，他们更喜欢从审美沉思的立场、在完全非宗教的参照框架中看待形象。“审美体验”的倡导者会主张：被视为宗教力量、救赎和精神振奋之源的形象，不是因其“美”、而是因完全不同的原因被欣赏。我认为这在两个理由上站不住脚。首先，我分不清宗教性的精神振奋与审美带来的精神振奋；在我看来，艺术爱好者在大多数相关意义上确实崇拜形象，并通过把事实上的偶像崇拜合理化为审美敬畏来为之开脱。因此，写艺术实际上就是写宗教，或者写那些放弃了既有宗教外在形式的人聊以安慰自己的宗教替代品。新教—清教遗产与一种特殊形式的艺术理论诡辩相结合，在当代西方世界确立了一种关于“形象的力量”的特殊形式的自欺，正如弗里德伯格（1989）令人信服地论证的（见下文）。我们通过把偶像重新归类为艺术而中和了它们；但我们在它们面前履行的敬礼，丝毫不亚于最虔诚的偶像崇拜者在其木神面前履行的敬礼——我明确把自己也包括在这一描述中。其次，从人类学观点看，我们必须承认，“审美态度”是启蒙运动宗教危机与西方科学兴起的一个特定历史产物，对没有像我们这样内化启蒙运动的文明不适用。在印度（它在随后的讨论中占很大分量），偶像崇拜作为一种宗教性形式繁荣兴盛，任何头脑正常的人都不会试图在受尊崇偶像的美的形式与宗教功能之间打入楔子。在印度，美学如同在古代世界一样，理所当然地被归入宗教哲学、即道德哲学之下。因此，美与神圣之间、宗教体验与审美体验之间的分离，只有从非常偏狭（戴眼罩）的西方后启蒙观点才会产生。既然如此，写艺术的人类学家必然对宗教人类学有所贡献，因为宗教——在某些语境中，虽非全部——先于艺术。
en: Granted that idolatry may be so called, I still have to explain why a book ostensibly about ‘art' has to devote so many pages to a topic which appears to belong to the study of religion rather than aesthetics. Those who object to my anti-aesthetics stance will regard as irrelevant the ‘religious function' of images they prefer to see in a totally non-religious frame of reference, from the standpoint of aesthetic contemplation. An image viewed as a source of religious power, salvation, exaltation, is not appreciated for its ‘beauty', but for quite different reasons, the proponents of ‘aesthetic experiences' would argue. I regard this as fallacious on two grounds. First of all, I cannot tell between religious and aesthetic exaltation; art-lovers, it seems to me, actually do worship images in most of the relevant senses, and explain away their de facto idolatry by rationalizing it as aesthetic awe. Thus, to write about art at all is, in fact, to write about either religion, or the substitute for religion which those who have abandoned the outward forms of received religions content themselves with. The Protestant-Puritan heritage combined with a special form of art-theoretical casuistry have established a special form of bad faith about the ‘power of images' in the contemporary Western world, as Freedberg (1989) has pursuasively argued (see below). We have neutralized our idols by reclassifying them as art; but we perform obeisances before them every bit as deep as those of the most committed idolater before his wooden god-I specifically include myself in this description. Secondly, from the anthropological point of view, we have to recognize that the ‘aesthetic attitude' is a specific historical product of the religious crisis of the Enlightenment and the rise of Western science, and that it has no applicability to civilizations which have not internalized the Enlightenment as we have. In India (which figures largely in the ensuing discussion) idolatry flourishes as a form of religiosity, and nobody in their right minds would try to drive a wedge between the beautiful form and religious function of venerated idols. In India aesthetics, as in the ancient world, is subsumed under the philosophy of religion, that is, moral philosophy, as a matter of course. Consequently, it is only from a very parochial (blinkered) Western post-Enlightenment point of view that the separation between the beautiful and the holy, between religious experience and aesthetic experience, arises. Since this is so, the anthropologist writing about art inevitably contributes to the anthropology of religion, because the religious is --in some contexts, though not all---prior to the artistic.

zh: 偶像有很多种类，但惯例是区分两个极性类型：（i）纯粹“无像的”偶像，如古希腊崇拜的拜图利亚（黑色陨石），与（ii）“有像的”偶像，即在形体上与原型（通常是人）相似的索引，按公式[[原型-A] → [艺术家-A]] ⟶ 索引-P

，其中原型是神，其“肖像”由艺术家中介。然而，在开始之前，不妨澄清我们不太重视这一区分的理由。我认为，所有偶像都是“有像的”——包括所谓无像的在内——无论它们是否看起来像某个熟悉对象，如人体。无像偶像是对神的“写实”表现：该神要么（在任何地方）没有形式，要么在下界为了被凡人信徒崇拜而栖居的特定“身体”中具有“任意”的形式。陨石不是一个在别处看起来像人的神的非常非常程式化或扭曲的“肖像”。不必想象拜石者会“更喜欢”崇拜其神的更写实的描绘，只是因为当地缺乏具备必要能力的石匠而不得不凑合用未成形的石头。对这样的崇拜者来说，陨石是神之时空在场（以及起源，因为石头从天而降）的索引。石头是神的“代表”，像大使，而不是视觉圣像。正如大使可以一年在莫斯科、次年在华盛顿代表其国家，石头在它碰巧所在的任何空间坐标代表神；而且它是可移动的。例如，这样一块在阿拉伯作为库柏勒受崇拜的“黑石”，被以盛大仪式运到罗马，安放进伊达山大母神偶像内的一个空腔中——这位女神是帝国精英中青睐“国际主义”宗教取向的成员的女神（Dumezil 1980；关于这类交易的意义，见下文）。“再现”（像图画）与“代表”（像大使）这两个观念是不同的，但仍然相联。大使是其国家在时空上分离出来的碎片，出国旅行，外国人可以与他交谈，“仿佛”在与他的国家政府交谈。尽管大使是真实的人，他们也是“虚构”，像图画一样，而他们的大使馆是国家之内虚构的迷你国家；正如图画向我们展示“并不真正在那里”的风景与人物。尽管中国驻伦敦大使看起来不像中国、中国政府或中国人民，他必须可见，而且他确实在官方场合可见地代表中国。他看起来不像中国，但在伦敦，中国看起来像他。
en: Idols come in many varieties, but it is conventional to distinguish two polar types; (i) purely ‘aniconic' idols, such as the baitulia (black meteoritic stones) worshipped in ancient Greece, versus (ii) ‘iconic' idols, that is, indexes physically resembling a prototype, usually a human being, according to the formula [[Prototype-A → [Artist-A]] ⟶ Index-P, where the prototype is the god, whose ‘likeness' is mediated by the artist. However, before starting, it may be as well to clarify our reasons for not paying very much attention to this distinction. All idols, I think, are ‘iconic’—including the so-called aniconic ones—whether or not they look like some familiar object, such as a human body. An aniconic idol is a ‘realistic' representation of a god who either has no form (anywhere), or has an ‘arbitrary' form, in the particular ‘body' he inhabits for the purposes of being worshipped by his mortal devotees, here below. A meteoritic stone is not a very, very, conventionalized or distorted ‘portrait' of a god, who, elsewhere, looks like a human being. One need not imagine that worshippers of stones would ‘prefer' to worship more realistic portrayals of their gods, but have to make do with unshaped stones for lack of any local stone-carvers of the necessary ability. For such worshippers, the meteoritic stone is an index of the god's spatio-temporal presence (and origins, in that the stone fell to earth from heaven). The stone is a ‘representative' of the god, like an ambassador, rather than a visual icon. Just as an ambassador can represent his country in Moscow one year, and the following year in Washington, the stone represents the god at whatever spatial coordinates it happens to be; and it is movable. One such ‘black stone' for instance, worshipped in Arabia as Cybele, was conveyed with great ceremony to Rome, where it was installed into a cavity within the idol of Magna Mater Idea, the goddess of members of the Imperial elite who favoured an ‘internationalist' religious outlook (Dumézil 1980; on the significance of such transactions, see below). The ideas of ‘representing' (like a picture) and ‘representing' (like an ambassador) are distinct, but none the less linked. An ambassador is a spatio-temporally detached fragment of his nation, who travels abroad and with whom foreigners can speak, ‘as if' they were speaking to his national government. Although ambassadors are real persons, they are also ‘fictions', like pictures, and their embassies are fictional mini-states within the state; just as pictures show us landscapes and personages who are ‘not really there'. Although the Chinese ambassador in London does not look like China, or the Chinese government or people, he does have to be visible, and he does visibly represent China on official occasions. He does not look like China, but in London, China looks like him.

zh: 人们不能把“写实的”有像大使与“不写实的”无像大使对立起来，同样，也许也不该把“写实的”偶像与不写实的无像偶像对立起来。无论偶像看起来像什么，在语境中那就是神的样子，所以所有偶像都同样写实，因为偶像形式就是在偶像中在场的神的视觉形式。对比不在于或多或少类似于人的偶像之间，而在于以偶像形式（视觉上）或多或少类似于人的神之间。换言之，偶像不是描绘、不是肖像，而是（人工制品的）身体。于是上面引用的公式[[原型-A] → [艺术家-A]] ⟶ 索引-P并不必然意味着艺术家以形象形式对原型作“写实的”（即拟人的）描绘。当这一公式应用于肖像画时，这一含义存在，因为肖像有一个活的模特，而忠实于这个活模特是肖像画的社会目标。但在偶像崇拜的语境中，所涉及的能动性是宗教性的。当偶像是人工制品（而非陨石之类的自然对象）时，原型所行使的能动性的性质，是使艺术家按照此类形象的惯例生产宗教规定的形象，这些惯例可能是有像的／拟人的，也可能是抽象而无像的。无论哪种情况，艺术家都必须“忠实”地再现神之身体的公认形象的特征，在其崇拜者中触发对神的“识别”。
en: One could not contrast a ‘realistic' iconic ambassador to an ‘unrealistic', aniconic ambassador, and no more, perhaps, should one contrast ‘realistic' idols, to unrealistic, aniconic idols. Whatever the idol looks like, that, in context, is what the god looks like, so all idols are equally realistic, because the idol-form is the visual form of the god made present in the idol. The contrast is not between idols which resemble human beings to a greater or lesser degree, but between gods who in idol-form (visually) resemble human beings to a greater or lesser degree. Idols, in other words, are not depictions, not portraits, but (artefactual) bodies. The formula cited above then [[Prototype-A → [Artist-A]] ⟶ Index-P does not necessarily imply ‘realistic' (i.e. anthropomorphic) depiction of the prototype by the artist in the form of the image. When such a formula is applied to portraiture, this implication exists, because there is a living model for the portrait, and fidelity to this living model is the social objective of portraiture. But in the context of idolatry, the agency involved is religious. Where an idol is an artefact (rather than a natural object, such as a meteoritic stone), the nature of agency exerted by the prototype is to cause the artist to produce a religiously stipulated image according to the conventions for such images, which may be iconic/anthropomorphic or abstract and aniconic. In either case, the artist has to produce a ‘faithful' rendition of the features of the accepted image of the body of the god, triggering ‘recognition' of the god among his worshippers.

zh: 断言在偶像崇拜语境中偶像不是神的“描绘”而是人工制品形式的神的身体，这固然好，但我承认任何这样的断言都构成悖论，我必须努力消除它在任何合理之人心中必然产生的困惑。偶像有生命之谜、它们真实（尽管奇特）的人格，必须像任何难题一样，经由一系列渐进步骤来接近，更不用说绕道一些陌生领域了。我不打算处理偶像崇拜最繁复的形式，而是通过分析模拟巫术（envoutement）——经由他人的形象加害于他人的实践——来引入这一主题。这是经由再现性索引中介的能动性的一个特别贴切的案例，而且它的好处是暂时把讨论从“严格意义上的宗教”领域移开，后者总是涉及神之类彼岸实体这一成问题的问题。模拟巫术发生在这个世界，不需要彼岸的神圣或恶魔干预，尽管可以寻求这种干预。正如我们将能观察到的，此世的模拟巫术与朝向彼岸存在的宗教偶像崇拜之间，实际上存在平滑的过渡。这将适时解释。
en: To assert that in the context of idolatry, the idol is not a ‘depiction' of the god, but the body of the god in artefact-form is all very well, but I accept that any such assertion constitutes a paradox, and I must labour hard to dispel the puzzlement it must inevitably produce in the mind of any reasonable person. The mystery of the animation of idols, their genuine, if peculiar, personhood, has to be approached, like any difficult problem, via a series of incremental steps, not to mention detours through some unfamiliar territory. Rather than deal with idolatry in its most elaborated form, I shall introduce the subject by presenting an analysis of volt sorcery (envoutement)-the practice of inflicting harm on others via their images. This is a particularly pertinent case of agency mediated via representational indexes, and it has the advantage of removing the discussion, temporarily, from the sphere of ‘religion proper', which involves the always problematic question of other-worldly entities such as gods. Volt sorcery takes place in this world and without the necessity for other-worldly divine or diabolic intervention, though it may be sought. As we will be able to observe, there is actually a smooth transition between this-worldly volt sorcery and religious image-worship orientated towards other-worldly beings. This will be explained in due course.

zh: 7.2　摹仿能力
en: 7.2　The Mimetic Faculty

zh: 这场讨论所承继的学术先驱是弗雷泽，而不是泰勒。回想一下，弗雷泽区分了“魔法”行动的两种基本模式：（i）接触巫术，即接触的魔法，影响从一个对象传递到另一个对象；（ii）交感巫术，依赖于共享属性，即如果对象A与对象B共享属性，A就对B有影响，反之亦然。弗雷泽关于“摹仿性”交感巫术的观念在20世纪对美学和艺术哲学产生了巨大影响。经由本雅明与阿多诺，这一影响似乎还将继续；陶西格（1993）在一本极其令人兴奋的新著中——其主要灵感来自本雅明——这样谈论弗雷泽：
en: Frazer, rather than Tylor, is the ancestral figure who presides over this discussion. Frazer, it will be recalled, distinguished two basic modes of ‘magical' action; (i) contagious magic, the magic of contact, in which influence passes from one object to another, and (ii) sympathetic magic, which depends on shared properties, that is, if object A shares properties with object B, A has influence over B or vice versa. The Frazerian idea of ‘imitative' sympathetic magic has had an enormous influence on aesthetics and the philosophy of art in the course of this century. Via Benjamin and Adorno, this influence seems set to continue; Taussig (1993) in a most exciting recent book, whose primary inspiration comes from Benjamin, has this to say about Frazer:

zh: 我特别被［弗雷泽的］这一命题所吸引：交感巫术的摹仿成分所依据的原则是“巫师推断，他只需摹仿任何他想要的效果，就能产生该效果”。（52）暂且搁置这个棘手问题：弗雷泽怎样才能从这些巫师中某个人的角度来想，又能在多大程度上做到这一点，以及他的命题的准确性或有用性在多大程度上依赖于这一步骤；我想仔细考察这样的观念：在魔法实践中，副本对原件的影响会达到如此程度，以至于再现物会分享或获得被再现者的属性。对我来说这是一个令人不安的观念，它陌生而迷人，不是因为它如此公然地与我周围的世界相矛盾，而是因为一旦提出这个观念，我便猜想，在我周围这个世界那些让人奇异地熟悉、寻常而无意识的再现习惯中，即使见不到它本身，也看得出它的蛛丝马迹。（Taussig 1993: 47-8）
en: I am particularly taken by [Frazer's] proposition that the principle underlying the imitative component of sympathetic magic is that ‘the magician infers that he can produce any effect he desires merely by imitating it'. (52) Leaving aside for the moment the thorny issue of how and with what success Frazer could put himself into the head of one of these magicians, and to what degree either the accuracy or usefulness of his proposition depends on such a move, I want to dwell on this notion of the copy, in magical practice, affecting the original to such a degree that the representation shares in or acquires the properties of the represented. To me this is a disturbing notion, foreign and fascinating not because it so flagrantly contradicts the world about me but rather, that once posited, I suspect if not its presence, then intimations thereof, in the strangely familiar commonplace and unconscious habits of representation in the world about me. (Taussig 1993: 47-8)

zh: 追随本雅明，陶西格把他在殖民环境（库纳印第安人）中对摹仿的分析建立在一种假定的“摹仿能力”上。本雅明认为，摹仿能力在现代造成了一个形象与拟像满溢的世界，以致任何东西都不再显得真实，而它起源于一种原始冲动，驱使人们摹仿世界并由此通达世界：
en: Following Benjamin, Taussig bases his analysis of mimesis in the colonial milieu (of the Cuna Indians) on a supposed ‘mimetic faculty'. Benjamin thought that the mimetic faculty, which in modern times has resulted in a world filled to overflowing with images and simulacra, so that nothing seems real any more, had its origin in a primitive compulsion to imitate, and thus gain access, to the world:

zh: ［人］看出相似之处的天赋，不过是往昔那种要变成别的东西、照那样东西的方式行事的强大冲动的残余。在人的各种高级机能中，也许每一项都有赖于摹仿能力所起的决定性作用。（1933；引自 Taussig 1993: 19）
en: [Man's] gift of seeing resemblances is nothing other than a rudiment of the powerful compulsion in former times to become and behave like something else. Perhaps there is none of his higher functions in which his mimetic faculty does not play a decisive role. (1933; cited in Taussig 1993: 19)

zh: 陶西格的书见证了弗雷泽的观念经由本雅明的超现实主义想象中介后的多产，但可以公允地说，“摹仿能力”只被相当含糊地勾勒。大量人类行为是摹仿性的，这一事实并不必然意味着存在一种从遥远过去继承下来的“能力”。几乎所有习得行为都可以被描述为摹仿性的，因为它基于对内化模型的摹仿。狭义定义的摹仿涉及形象（索引）的实际生产，它们最显著的属性是凭借与原物的相似，显出其原型；在这一范畴内，与原件具有视觉相似性的人工制品可以被赋予单独的地位。
en: Taussig's book bears witness to the productivity of Frazer's idea mediated through Benjamin's surrealist imagination, but it is fair to say that the ‘mimetic faculty' is only rather vaguely delineated. The fact that so much human behaviour is imitative does not necessarily imply the existence of a ‘faculty' inherited from the distant past. Almost all learned behaviour could be described as imitative, in that it is based on the imitation of an internalized model. Mimesis, narrowly defined, involves the actual production of images (indexes) whose salient property is prototype, via resemblance to the original, and within this category artefacts, having visual resemblance to the originals, can be accorded a separate status.

zh: 弗雷泽从未解释的是：为什么形象与原件的相互相似应该成为相互影响或能动性的管道。他把它归于一个错误的假说，类似于科学理论但基于错误。麻烦在于：如果交感巫术的实践者能像弗雷泽那样看待自己的实践，他们一开始就绝不会从事这些实践。通过从混沌的实践世界中抽象出可概括的“原则”，弗雷泽的做法注定会使他误解手头的材料。陶西格在其本雅明式的重新分析中论证，交感巫术的基础不是对物理因果性质的悲剧性误解，而是认知觉知本身的结果。看（或知）就是被感知之物感性地充满，向它屈服、映照它——从而在身体上摹仿它（同上 45）（见上文“摄魅”，第5.2节）。但眼下我将从另一个方向接近交感巫术问题。
en: What Frazer never explained is why the mutual resemblance of the image and the original should be a conduit for mutual influence or agency. He attributed it to a mistaken hypothesis, akin to a scientific theory, but grounded in error. The trouble is that if the practitioners of sympathetic magic could have seen their practices as Frazer saw them, they would never have engaged in them in the first place. By abstracting a generalizable ‘principle' from the inchoate world of practice, Frazer guaranteed his eventual misunderstanding of the data he had at his disposal. Taussig, in his Benjaminesque reanalysis, argues that the basis of sympathetic magic is not a tragic misunderstanding of the nature of physical causality, but a consequence of epistemic awareness itself. To see (or to know) is to be sensuously filled with that which is perceived, yielding to it, mirroring it—and hence imitating it bodily (ibid. 45) (see above in ‘Captivation', Sect. 5.2). But for the moment I will approach the sympathetic magic problem from a different direction.

zh: 弗雷泽的理智主义把魔法当作一种错误的因果思维。此后的反弗雷泽派一直批评弗雷泽把“因果”意图归于象征性或表达性行为（Beattie 1966）。不过还有另一种可采取的进路：不是谴责弗雷泽竟然诉诸因果性（因为魔法毕竟意在使事情发生），而是重新思考“原因”的观念。弗雷泽的错误在于把一种伪科学的物理因果观念（涵盖整个宇宙）强加于依赖意向性与目的的实践，而意向性与目的恰恰是科学决定论所缺失的。魔法之所以可能，是因为意图使事件在施动者周边发生，但这是一种不同于太阳升落、牛顿苹果落地等所涉及的那种因果的因果类型。例如：我面前有这个煮鸡蛋。是什么使这个鸡蛋被煮熟？显然有两个完全不同的答案——（i）因为它在煤气火焰上的一锅水中被加热；（ii）因为我自己拿定主意，动手从盒子里取出鸡蛋，往锅里加水，点着煤气，煮鸡蛋，因为我想吃早餐。从任何实践观点看，鸡蛋被煮熟的第（ii）类“原因”都远比第（i）类重要。如果周围没有像我这样想要早餐的施动者，就不会有鸡蛋（除了东南亚丛林里），不会有锅，不会有煤气器具，整个煮蛋现象就永远不会发生，也永远不需要物理解释。所以，无论物理学作何裁决，为什么会有煮鸡蛋的真正因果解释是：我和其他吃早餐的人意图让煮鸡蛋存在。
en: Frazer's intellectualism treated magic as a form of mistaken causal thinking. Anti-Frazerians, ever since, have criticized Frazer for attributing ‘causal' intentions to behaviours which were symbolic or expressive (Beattie 1966). There is another approach, though, which can be adopted, which is not to condemn Frazer for having invoked causality at all (because magic is, after all, intended to cause things to happen) but to rethink the idea of ‘cause'. Frazer's mistake was to impose a pseudo-scientific notion of physical cause and effect (encompassing the entire universe) on practices which depend on intentionality and purpose, which is precisely what is missing from scientific determinism. Magic is possible because intentions cause events to happen in the vicinity of agents, but this is a different species of causation from the kind of causation involved in the rising and setting of the sun, or the falling of Newton's apple etc. For instance: here before me is this boiled egg. What has caused this egg to be boiled? Clearly, there are two quite different answers to this-(i) because it was heated in a saucepan of water over a gas-flame, or (ii) because I, off my own bat, chose to bestir myself, take the egg from its box, fill the saucepan, light the gas, and boil the egg, because I wanted breakfast. From any practical point of view, type-(ii) ‘causes' of eggs being boiled are infinitely more salient than type-(i) causes. If there were no breakfast-desiring agents like me about, there would be no hens' eggs (except in the South-East Asian jungle), no saucepans, no gas appliances, and the whole egg-boiling phenomenon would never transpire and never need to be physically explained. So, whatever the verdict of physics, the real causal explanation for why there are any boiled eggs is that I, and other breakfasters, intend that boiled eggs should exist.

zh: 把自己周边事件的因果追溯到自己或附近其他施动者的意图，或他们某种意愿与愿望的表达，并不涉及任何神秘的东西。完全普通的事件通常就是这样发生的——除非“意外”，而谁又能知道某个意外不是某人所希望发生的呢？弗雷泽的错误可以说在于想象巫师持有某种非标准的物理理论，而真相是：“魔法”就是当你以物理理论多余为由而不要它时所得到的东西，它依赖一个完全可行的观念：任何给定事件（尤其在社会上显著的事件）的解释是它被有意地引起。
en: There is nothing mystical involved in tracing the causation of events in one's vicinity to intentions or acts of willing or wishing performed by oneself or other agents in one's neighbourhood. That is how perfectly ordinary events do ordinarily happen-barring ‘accidents', and who is ever to know that an accident has not been willed by somebody? Frazer's mistake was, so to speak, to imagine that magicians had some non-standard physical theory, whereas the truth is that ‘magic' is what you have when you do without a physical theory on the grounds of its redundancy, relying on the idea, which is perfectly practicable, that the explanation of any given event (especially if socially salient) is that it is caused intentionally.

zh: 愿望与愿望实现之间的因果箭头反映了这一实践事实：一个人越想要某事发生，它就越可能发生（尽管仍可能不发生）。魔法把愿望的强烈程度标明并公之于众，使人们强烈希望、且郑重说出口的事情更可能成真，这种可能性得到归纳经验的支持，正如我们大声疾呼要求的结果常常发生的那样。“一切事件之所以发生，是因为有人希望它发生”——“我强烈希望 X 发生”，所以“X必将实现”。这不是“混乱的”物理学，也并非没有社会经验的基础，马林诺夫斯基（1935）比他的任何后继者都更清楚地理解这一点，可能的例外是坦比亚（1985）。
en: The causal arrow between desire and accomplishment reflects the practical fact that the more one desires something to happen, the more likely it is to happen (though it still may not). Magic registers and publicizes the strength of desire, increasing the (inductively supported) likelihood that the much-desired, emphatically expressed, outcome will transpire, as frequently happens with respect to those outcomes we loudly clamour for. ‘All events happen because they are intended'-'I emphatically intend that X shall happen' ergo ‘X shall come to pass'. This is not ‘confused' physics, nor is it devoid of a basis in social experience, as Malinowski (1935) understood more clearly than any of his successors, with the possible exception of Tambiah (1985).

zh: 7.3　模拟巫术
en: 7.3　Volt Sorcery

zh: 本文前几节发展的符号语言可以应用于弗雷泽交感（摹仿）巫术首要例子所涉及的因果类型——陶西格也广泛讨论过——即制作受害者形象（常用蜡或某种易损材料）、加以伤害或毁灭，结果巫术的受害者遭受同样伤害或被彻底消灭的那种巫术形式。这种巫术在世界各地以无数形式实践，任何翻开弗雷泽的书的人都能发现。
en: The symbolic language developed in earlier sections of this essay can be applied to the kind of causality which is involved in Frazer's prime example of sympathetic (imitative) magic, which is also extensively discussed by Taussig, namely, that form of sorcery in which an image of the victim is made (often of wax or some vulnerable material), subjected to injury or destruction, with the result that the victim of the sorcery suffers the same injuries or is done away with entirely. This kind of sorcery is practised in innumerable forms, all over the world, as anyone who opens Frazer's book is able to discover.

zh: 这种巫术可以以无像形式实践；例如古希腊人过去常常互相施巫：取小铅片，在上面刻下受害者的名字和“我缚住，我缚住”字样，然后埋入地下。他们相信这会使受害者染病而死。与用受害者形象代替刻字铅片的模拟巫术相比较是有趣的，因为它暗示“视觉再现”与“束缚”（以及命名）本质上相近。“束缚”确实是魔法—宗教控制的一个基本隐喻，我们下文还会遇到。“我缚住，我缚住”这句话在魔法的语言面（它们是词语）与物理面（它们指涉在受害者身体上执行的物理操作）之间提供了桥梁。制作任何种类的再现性形象的行为都涉及某种束缚，因为原型的形象被系于索引，或被固定、囚禁于索引之内。
en: This kind of sorcery can be practised in aniconic forms; the ancient Greeks, for instance, used to sorcerize one another by taking small pieces of lead, on which they would scratch the name of the victim, and the words ‘I bind, I bind' before burying them in the ground. This would cause the victim to sicken and die. The comparison with volt sorcery, which uses the image of the victim in place of the inscribed lead is interesting, in that it suggests that ‘visual representation' and ‘binding' (and naming) are essentially akin to one another. ‘Binding' is, indeed, a fundamental metaphor of magico-religious control which we will encounter below. The words ‘I bind, I bind' provide a bridge between the linguistic side of magic (they are words) and the physical side of magic (they refer to a physical operation, carried out on the body of the victim). The action of making a representational image, of any kind, involves a kind of binding, in that the image of the prototype is bound to, or fixed and imprisoned within, the index.

zh: 对被表现于索引（照片或肖像）中的紧张不安，常被讨论得仿佛它只是天真部落民的怪癖——他们相信自己的灵魂有在其中被偷走的危险。事实上，几乎每个人都有理由希望在某种程度上控制别人怎样呈现自己，而不是任其自由流通。我也许认了让自己的脸被拍照、流通，但对我裸露的屁股就不这么想了。无须诉诸魔法或万物有灵论信仰来证实这一观念：人确实极易受到经由形象的敌意表现的伤害，不只是残酷的漫画，甚至完全中性的描绘，只要它们被以轻蔑或嘲笑对待。问题不只是被表现于形象中的人经由纯粹象征或约定的联系与该形象“认同”；而是因为被表现者的能动性实际印刻在表现之上。我是我的表现所采取的形式的原因，我对它负责。我不能以我没有按快门、没有使这个损害性形象存在为由，否认一张我难看屁股的照片。我可以怪摄影师拍了这张照片，但不能因为自己在照片里是那副样子就怪他。
en: Nervousness about being represented in an index (a photograph or portrait) is often discussed as if it were only a foible of innocent tribesmen, who believe that their souls are in danger of being stolen away therein. In fact, almost everyone has reasons for wishing to keep some degree of control over representations of themselves, rather than have them circulate freely. I might be resigned to having my face photographed and circulated, but I do not feel the same about my naked behind. There is no reason to invoke magical or animistic beliefs in order to substantiate the idea that persons are very vulnerable indeed to hostile representation via images, not just to cruel caricatures, but even via perfectly neutral portrayals, if these are treated with contumely or ridicule. It is not just that the person represented in an image is ‘identified' with that image via a purely symbolic or conventional linkage; rather, it is because the agency of the person represented is actually impressed on the representation. I am the cause of the form that my representation takes, I am responsible for it. I cannot disown a photograph of my inelegant posterior, on the grounds that I did not press the shutter and cause this damaging image to come into existence. I can blame the photographer for taking the picture, but I cannot blame him for the way the picture came out.

zh: 模拟巫术的“魔法”方面只是我们与巫师和受害者疏离、无法充分设身处地理解他们所产生的附带现象，而不是他们被与我们完全不同的迷信信仰奴役的结果。我们作为受动者，遭受经由我们自己的形象中介的能动性形式的伤害，因为作为社会人，我们不仅在场于我们单一的身体中，而且在场于我们周围一切见证我们的存在、属性与能动性的事物中。模拟巫术只是更照字面去利用人能够被再现为图像这一处境。它并不诉诸某种神秘力量、某种魔法因果原则而离开日常世界；相反，它把因与果结合得过于紧密，以致连接形象与被表现者的因果纽带变得可逆——形象可以朝相反方向对人施加因果效果。模拟巫术的操作方式可以用前面引入的图示约定很容易地表达，可见[

en: The ‘magical' aspect of volt sorcery is only an epiphenomenon of our failure to identify sufficiently with sorcerers and their victims, our estrangement from them, not the result of their enslavement by superstitious beliefs entirely different from our own. We suffer, as patients, from forms of agency mediated via images of ourselves, because, as social persons, we are present, not just in our singular bodies, but in everything in our surroundings which bears witness to our existence, our attributes, and our agency. Volt sorcery is not a more magical but just a more literal-minded exploitation of the predicament of representability in image form. It does not take leave of the everyday world, in appealing to some occult force, some magical principle of causation; on the contrary, it unites cause and effect all too closely, so that the causal nexus linking the image to the person represented is made reversible-the image can exercise a causal effect, in the opposite direction, over the person. The modus operandi of volt sorcery can readily be expressed using the diagrammatic conventions introduced earlier, as in Fig 7.3/1, or:

zh: 可以说，模拟巫术的逼真性在于受害者出现两次：一次作为使索引采取其特定形式的原型，一次作为接受者，其伤害源于索引所受的伤害。受害者经由迂回的因果路径，最终是自己能动性的受害者。脆弱性源于表现的纯粹可能性，而这无法避免。巫术信仰持存且极具解释力，因为对巫术的脆弱性是人经由千百种因果影响与路径扩散到环境中所产生的非意图后果，而这些影响与路径并非都能被监控和控制。弗雷泽自己注意到，基于形象的巫术与依赖蜕余物的另一种巫术紧密结盟：头发、剪下的指甲、食物残渣、排泄物之类。通常，把受害者的蜕余物纳入模拟像会使模拟巫术更有效，于是基于（视觉）相似的摹仿巫术就与基于接触的另一种主要魔法结盟。再一次，把这描述为“魔法”并想象这种巫术基于神秘原则（或象征仪式）是相当误导的。蜕余物巫术所涉及的因果类型没有任何超验之处，尽管巫师在追索其仇恨对象时常常可能征召灵性帮手。蜕余物巫术起作用（或似乎可能起作用），是因为蜕余物与留下这些东西的人之间的紧密因果纽带。这些蜕余物不是转喻地代表受害者；它们是受害者“分布式人格”——即分布于环境中、超出身体边界的人格——在物理上分离的碎片。
en: The verisimilitude, so to speak, of volt sorcery resides in the fact that the victim appears twice; once as the prototype who causes the index to assume its particular form, and once as the recipient, whose injuries stem from the injuries that the index has received. The victim is ultimately the victim of his own agency, by a circuitous causal pathway. Vulnerability stems from the bare possibility of representation, which cannot be avoided. Sorcery beliefs endure, and are highly explanatory, because vulnerability to sorcery is the unintended consequence of the diffusion of the person into the milieu, via a thousand causal influences and pathways, not all of which can be monitored and controlled. Frazer himself noted that image-based sorcery is closely allied to the other kind of sorcery which depends on exuviae; hair, nail-clippings, food leftovers, excreta, and the like. Often, the volt is rendered more effective by the incorporation into it of the victim's exuviae, so that imitative magic, based on (visual) similarity, is allied with the other main kind of magic, based on contact. Once again, to describe this as ‘magic' and to imagine that such sorcery is based on occult principles (or symbolic rituals) is quite misleading. There is nothing transcendental about the kind of causality involved in exuviae sorcery, though often sorcerers may enlist spiritual helpers in pursuing the objects of their hatred. Exuviae sorcery works (or seems likely to work) because of the intimate causal nexus between exuviae and the person responsible for them. These exuviae do not stand metonymically for the victim; they are physically detached fragments of the victim's ‘distributed personhood'-that is, personhood distributed in the milieu, beyond the body-boundary.

zh: 从我们的观点看，蜕余物巫术的趣味在于它在作为原型形象的索引与作为原型（分离）部分的索引之间锻造了直接联系。我们不习惯把形象（如肖像等）思考为人的部分，仿佛肢体。就表现的符号学理论而言，没有什么比想象符号的实体（可见或可听的符号“狗”）是任何狗或一般狗的部分更错误的了。但索引与严格意义上的符号不同。从索引出发的溯因推理确实特征性地涉及设定一种实质的部分—整体（或部分—部分）关系。例如，烟是火的一种“部分”。一个人的微笑（柴郡猫除外）是它所标示的友好之人的部分。从这一观点看，假设康斯太布尔画的索尔兹伯里大教堂是索尔兹伯里大教堂的部分，并非没有意义。它是我们所谓的从索尔兹伯里大教堂衍生出来的东西。
en: The interest of exuviae sorcery, from our point of view, is that it forges a direct link between the index as an image of the prototype, and the index as a (detached) part of the prototype. We are not accustomed to think of images (such as portraits, etc.) as parts of persons, limbs, as it were. In terms of the semiotic theory of representation, nothing would be more erroneous than to imagine that the substance of a sign (the visible or audible sign ‘dog') were part of any dog, or dogs in general. But with indexes it is not the same as with proper signs. Abduction from an index does characteristically involve positing a substantive part-whole (or part part) relation. Smoke is a kind of ‘part' of fire, for instance. A person's smile (the cheshire cat excepted) is a part of the friendly person it betokens. From this point of view, it is not senseless to suppose that Constable's picture of Salisbury cathedral is a part of Salisbury cathedral. It is, what we would call, a ‘spin-off' of Salisbury cathedral.

zh: 7.4　作为身体部分的“飞散拟像”的伊壁鸠鲁理论
en: 7.4　The Epicurean Theory of Flying Simulacra as Parts of the Body

zh: 物的形象与物的部分之间的汇合可以从哲学角度接近。于尔耶·希尔恩（1900，被弗雷泽1980引用，陶西格1993: 51也讨论过）提出：相似魔法与接触魔法实际上是同一种东西，因为“原始”人在其混乱中预先触及了“流溢”的哲学学说。希尔恩写道：
en: The convergence between images of things and parts of things can be approached from a philosophical angle. Yrjö Hirn (1900, cited by Frazer 1980 and discussed also by Taussig 1993: 51) made the suggestion that the magic of similarity and the magic of contact were really one and the same, because ‘primitive' people anticipated, in their confusion, the philosophical doctrine of ‘emanations'. Hirn writes:

zh: 因为显然，一种哲学学说如果与原始迷信的事实相契合，就可能解释那些没有逻辑证成或系统安排、存在于巫师与偶像崇拜者心中的含糊而潜在观念。这样一种学说呈现在我们熟悉的流溢理论中：按该理论，物的每一个形象都构成该物本身的一个具体部分。按照古代伊壁鸠鲁哲学家对这一学说的清晰而系统的陈述［我将在下文提供卢克莱修的相关引文］，影子、镜中反射、幻象、甚至远处对象的心理表象，都是由薄膜引起的，这些薄膜不断从所有物体的表面脱离，并在空间中朝所有方向前行。如果存在所谓必然的误解，这无疑是其中之一。反射、影子、海市蜃楼这类感性经验的一般事实，自然会显得是纯粹物质性的表层剥离的结果——就像转印画一样。这一理论甚至对现代心灵也可能近在咫尺，从一个奇怪的事实可以看出：像巴尔扎克这样的人在试图解释新发明的达盖尔银版摄影——最奇妙的形象现象——时，也求助于它。（Hirn 1900: 293-4；关于照片作为人之真实在场的索引，参 Barthes 1981，被 Freedberg 1989: 第15章引用并讨论）
en: For it is evident that a philosophical doctrine, if it fits in with the facts of primitive superstition, may be explanatory of those vague and latent notions which, without logical justification or systematical arrangement, lie in the mind of the magician and the idolater. Such a doctrine is presented to us in the familiar emanation-theories, according to which every image of a thing constitutes a concrete part of that thing itself. According to the clear and systematic statement of this doctrine given by the old Epicurean philosophers [I will provide the relevant quotation from Lucretius below] shadows, reflections in a mirror, visions, and even mental representations of distant objects, are all caused by thin membranes, which continually detach themselves from the surfaces of all bodies and move onwards in all directions through space. If there are such things as necessary misconceptions, this is certainly one. Such general facts of sensuous experience as reflection, shadow, and mirage will naturally appear as the result of a purely material decortication- as in a transfer picture. How near at hand this theory may lie even to the modern mind appears from the curious fact that such a man as Balzac fell back on it when attempting to explain the newly invented Daguerrotype, that most marvellous of image-phenomena. (Hirn 1900: 293–4; cf. on photographs as indexes of the real presence of persons, Barthes 1981 cited and discussed in Freedberg 1989: ch. 15)

zh: 流溢学说直接来自伊壁鸠鲁，但该学说最著名、且就我的目的而言最有趣的陈述由卢克莱修提供，他写道：
en: The doctrine of emanations comes directly from Epicurus, but the most famous, and for my purposes the most interesting, statement of the doctrine is provided by Lucretius, who writes:

zh: 我将试着向你说明一个至关紧要的真理……那就是我们称为事物之“像”［simulacra；希腊语 eidola］的那些东西大多确实存在：这些像像从物表面剥下的薄膜，在空气中来回飞……于是我说，事物的图像与薄薄的形体从物的表面发出，形象充当一种薄膜，或者你愿意叫它外皮也行，因为这种形象带有与它从其身体脱落并漫游而出的那个物相似的外观与形式。无论理解力多么迟钝，你都能从下文学到这一点。［许多可见对象］……发出物体，有些处于松散扩散状态，像橡木柴、热与火发出的烟；有些质地更紧密更浓，像蝉有时在夏天蜕下的薄纱衣，像牛犊出生时从身体表面脱落的薄膜，以及滑溜的蛇在荆棘间蜕下的衣；因为我们常常看到荆棘丛缀满它们飞落的战利品：既然这些情况发生，同样，薄的形象也必须从物的表面发出。（《物性论》4: 26 ff.，Munro 译，pp. 44-5）
en: I will attempt to lay before you a truth which most concerns ... the existence of most things we call the idols [simulacra; in Greek, eidola] of things: these, like films peeled off from the surface of things, fly to and fro through the air ... I say then that pictures of things and thin shapes are emitted from things off their surface, to which an image serves as a kind of film, or name it if you like a rind, because such image bears an appearance and form like to the thing whatever it is from whose body it is shed and wanders forth. This you may learn however dull of apprehension from what follows. [Many visible objects], . . . emit bodies some in a state of loose diffusion, like smoke which logs of oak, heat and fires emit; some of a closer and denser texture, like the gossamer coats which at times cicades doff in summer, and the films which calves at their birth cast from the surface of their body, as well as the vesture which the slippery serpent puts off among the thorns; for often we see the brambles enriched with their flying spoils: since these cases occur, a thin image likewise must be emitted from things off their surface. (De Rerum Natura 4: 26 ff. trans. Munro, pp. 44-5)

zh: 卢克莱修把物的飞散拟像归于物体内部的微粒相互推挤，它使“前排”的微小物体从表面被排出、向外飞。但拟像是物理的东西，我们看见对象是因为拟像进入我们的眼睛，而且我们能感觉到它们，“既然黑暗中用手摸到的那个形体，与明亮日光下所见的形体是同一个，触觉与视觉必定由相当相似的原因激起”。卢克莱修讨论了若干光学现象，尤其是镜子反射的形象，但也许最有趣的是他一贯在借助事物之“像”的视觉与向环境扩散的其他物理形式——尤其是气味与烟，以及从物表面脱落皮、壳、膜——之间作类比的方式。我后面将有机会回到烟、气味、皮与视觉外观之间的概念联系，库希勒已把这些认定为与一种特别著名的美拉尼西亚艺术形式——新不列颠北部的马兰甘雕刻——相联系的意识形态的关键要素（见下文第9.2节）。但眼下我感兴趣的是希尔恩的论点：如果物的“外观”是物的物质部分，那么，凭借接触一个人或一件物的图像而取得的支配力，与凭接触其某个物质部分所取得的支配力相当，甚至可以说是一回事；尤其当我们引入人可能是“分布式的”这一观念时，即人的各个“部分”不必全都附在身体上，还有一些散布在周遭环境中，像卢克莱修令人难忘的例子中蝉蜕下的“薄纱衣”——它们既是活物的形象又是活物的部分。
en: Lucretius attributes the flying simulacra of things to a kind of internal jostling within objects, which causes the minute bodies 'in the front rank' to be discharged from the surface and to fly outwards. The simulacra are physical things though, and we see objects because simulacra enter our eyes and we can feel them ‘since a particular figure felt by the hands in the dark is known to be the same which is seen by the bright light of day, touch and sight must be excited by quite similar causes'. Lucretius discusses a number of optical phenomena, notably images reflected by mirrors, but most interesting, perhaps, is the way in which he consistently draws analogies between vision by means of ‘idols' and other physical forms of diffusion into the ambience, particularly smell and smoke, as well as the shedding of skins, rinds, and films from the surfaces of things. I shall have occasion, later, to return to the conceptual linkage between smoke, smell, skins, and visual appearances, which Kuchler has identified as key elements in the ideology associated with a particularly well-known Melanesian art form, the Malangan carvings from northern New Britain (see below, Sect. 9.2). For the moment, though, I am interested in Hirn's point that if ‘appearances' of things are material parts of things, then the kind of leverage which one obtains over a person or thing by having access to their image is comparable, or really identical, to the leverage which can be obtained by having access to some physical part of them; especially if we introduce the notion that persons may be ‘distributed', i.e. all their ‘parts' are not physically attached, but are distributed around the ambience, like the discarded ‘gossamer coats of cicadas' in Lucretius' memorable instance, which are both images and parts of the living creature.

zh: 7.5　从巫术到图像崇拜
en: 7.5　From Sorcery to the Cult of Images

zh: 现在我要转向一个民族志例子，它在模拟巫术——这无疑是一种不光彩的行径——与宗教中的图像崇拜之间架起了一座桥梁。模拟巫术为理解一般的图像崇拜提供了一个模型——实际上也为宗教语境中一般的“对象化”提供了模型。材料——以及思路——来自阿兰·巴巴赞对古代塔希提宗教实践及其中形象之运用的出色再分析。
en: I turn now to an ethnographic example which provides a bridge between volt sorcery, surely a discreditable practice, and the worship of images in the religious context. Volt sorcery provides a model for understanding the worship of images in general-indeed for 'objectification' in religious contexts generally. The material-and the idea-comes from Alain Babadzan's remarkable reanalysis of the religious practices of ancient Tahiti, and the deployment of images therein.

zh: 也许已经有人注意到，模拟巫术的受害者被卷入了一种非自愿的交换过程。这自然源于他在公式中出现了两次：一次作为某物（他的外貌）的提供者，一次作为某物（与巫术偶人即索引所受的损伤相对应的损伤）的接受者。他是一个“非自愿的”施动者；自愿的能动性掌握在巫师手中——当然，巫师也可能确实有理由，毕竟他也许受到了挑衅。
en: It may have been noticed that the victim of volt sorcery is involved in an involuntary process of exchange. This arises naturally from the fact that he appears twice in the formula, once as the contributor of something (his appearance) and once as the recipient of something (injuries matching those suffered by the volt, the index). He is an ‘involuntary' agent; voluntary agency lies with the sorcerer-who may, of course, have been justifiably provoked.

zh: 巴巴赞对波利尼西亚巫术与偶像崇拜的论述之所以独具创见，在于他以一种微妙的方式观察到：这两者都是对那个著名却常令人困惑的交换过程解释的变体——那是毛利知识分子拉纳皮里向埃尔斯登·贝斯特所作的解释（参见 Mauss 1954; Sahlins 1974）。
en: The originality of Babadzan's account of Polynesian sorcery and idolatry arises from the subtle way in which he has observed both of these were variations on the well-known, but often tantalizing, explanation of the process of exchange provided by Ranapiri, the Maori intellectual, to Elsdon Best (cf. Mauss 1954; Sahlins 1974).

zh: 现在我要谈谈豪（hau），以及供豪（whangai hau）仪式。这个豪不是吹拂的风那个豪——完全不是。我要仔细向你解释。假设你拥有某件物品，你无偿地把这件物品给了我。我们没有就此讨价还价。现在，我把这件物品给了第三个人，过了一段时间，他决定为此作出回报，于是送了我某件物品。现在，他给我的这件物品，就是我先前从你那里收到、然后又给了他的那件物品的豪。我为那件物品收到的财物，我必须转交给你。我把这样的财物留给自己是不对的，无论它们是令人想要的东西还是别的什么。我必须把它们转交给你，因为它们是你给我的那件物品的豪……
en: I will now speak of the hau, and the ceremony of whangai hau. That hau is not the hau (wind) that blows-not at all. I will carefully explain to you. Suppose that you possess a certain article, and that you give that article to me, without price. We make no bargain over it. Now, I give that article to a third person, who, after some time has elapsed, decides to make some return for it, and so he makes me a present of some article. Now, that article he gives me is the hau of the article I first received from you and then gave to him. The goods that I received for that item I must hand over to you. It would not be right for me to keep such goods for myself, whether they be desirable items or otherwise. I must hand them over to you, because they are a hau of the article you gave me ...

zh: 我要向你解释一些关于森林之豪的事情。毛里（mauri）是由托洪加（tohunga）放置或植入森林中的。正是毛里使森林中鸟类繁多，使人得以捕杀获取。这些鸟是毛里的财产，属于毛里……因此人们说，应当向森林之豪献祭。托洪加（祭司、行家）吃下祭品，因为毛里是他们的：是他们把它安放在森林中，使它存在的。正因如此，在圣火上烹熟的鸟有一些被单独留出，只供祭司食用，以便森林物产之豪与毛里能够再次回到森林——也就是回到毛里。（Best 1909: 439）
en: I will explain something to you about the forest hau. The mauri was placed or implanted in the forest by the tohunga. It is the mauri that causes birds to be abundant in the forest, that they be slain and taken by man. These birds are the property of, belong to, the mauri ... Hence it is said that offerings should be made to the hau of the forest. The tohunga (priests, adepts) eat the offering because the mauri is theirs: it was they who located it in the forest, who caused it to be. That is why some of the birds cooked at the sacred fire are set apart to be eaten by the priests only, in order that the hau of the forest-products, and the mauri, may return again to the forest—that is, to the mauri. (Best 1909: 439)

zh: 巴巴赞解释说，拉纳皮里文本所描述的交换过程涉及三方参与者：祭司（托洪加）、“森林之豪”与猎人。“森林之豪”可以释读为森林的“增殖原理”；换言之，即森林的丰产力。祭司向森林之豪献上毛里作为祭品。森林之豪则以供猎人捕获的鸟作为回应。这些鸟必须有一部分返还给祭司。祭司所献、被称为毛里的祭品是“丰产石”。毛里在拉纳皮里的著名文本与本章主题之间建立了联系，因为毛里是无像的偶像。换言之，它们是索引：它们是森林（增殖）之灵的对象化贮存所。它们可能只是一些特殊的石头，但贝斯特还告诉我们，有时它们采取“一块中空石头的形式，空腔里会放上一绺头发或其他物品。这些物品会被安放在树根处，或藏在洞里，或放在树旁”（同上，438）。另一种毛里是把一只（活的）蜥蜴封砌在捕鸟地点旁的空心树里制成的（同上，437）。毛里偶像之中空性的意义将在适当的时候显现（见下文第7.11节）。
en: Babadzan explains that the exchange process described in Ranapiri's text involves three participants, the priests (tohunga), the ‘hau of the forest', and the hunters. The ‘hau of the forest' can be glossed as the ‘principle of increase' in the forest; its fertility in other words. The priests make offerings of mauri to the hau of the forest. The hau of the forest responds by providing the hunters with birds to capture. A portion of these birds must be returned to the priests. The offering made by the priests and referred to as mauri are ‘fertility stones'. The mauri forge the link between Ranapiri's famous text and our theme in this chapter, for mauri are aniconic idols. They are indexes, in other words: they are objectified repositories of the spirit (of increase) of the forest. They might just be special stones, but Best also tells us that sometimes they took the form of ‘a hollow stone, in which hollow would be placed a lock of hair or some other item. These articles would be deposited at the base of a tree, or hidden in a hole, or by the side of a tree' (ibid. 438). Another form of mauri was created by immuring a (living) lizard within a hollow tree beside a bird-snaring site (ibid. 437). The significance of the hollowness of mauri idols will emerge in due course (below, Sect. 7.11).

zh: 让我们回到巴巴赞对仪式序列的阐述：毛利猎人因在森林中捕获了鸟，有义务以所得猎物的一部分酬报祭司（托洪加）。
en: Let us return to Babadzan's exposition of the ritual sequence, in which, in exchange for the birds they captured in the forest, Maori hunters were obliged to recompense the priests (tohunga) with a portion of the game they secured.

zh: “魔法石与猎人所捕获的鸟，因此在仪式上是同一件事物，是同一件塔翁加（taonga，礼物），由祭司经由森林的中介能动性‘给予’猎人。”（Babadzan 1993: 64，我的翻译）
en: The magic stones and the birds the hunters capture are thus, ritually, one and the same thing, one and the same toanga (gift) that the priests ‘give' to the hunters, via the intermediary agency of the forest. (Babadzan 1993: 64, my trans.)

zh: 换言之，森林有义务把鸟给猎人，因为它的生命、它显现生产力与丰产力的能力并不属于它自己；那是祭司安放在那里的。“森林之豪——在毛利理论中，它同时正是森林生产力的原理本身——因此被视为一次传递中的被动施动者，而祭司是这次传递的发起者”（同上，斜体为原文所有，我的翻译）。但这里有一个悖论。一片森林——或任何别的东西——怎么可能是一个“被动的施动者”？从某种意义上说，这是一个措辞上的矛盾，因为被动性被定义为能动性的缺席，反之亦然。其含义是：森林相对于作为发起者的祭司是被动的，但并非说它完全没有内在的能动性。之所以能有森林的毛里——森林生产力的物质对象化——是因为森林本身就（潜在地）具有生产力；正是这种“能动性”被祭司的能动性所征用。
en: In other words, the forest is obliged to give birds to the hunters, because its life, its capacity to manifest productivity and fertility, is not its own; it has been placed there by the priests. ‘The hau of the forest, which meanwhile is, in Maori theory, the very principle of the productivity of the forest, is thus considered as the passive agent in a transmission of which the priests are the prime movers' (ibid., italics in original, my translation). But there is a paradox here. How can a forest, or anything else for that matter, be a ‘passive agent'-in a sense, this is a contradiction in terms, as passivity is defined as the absence of agency, and vice versa. What is meant is that the forest is passive in relation to the priests, the prime movers, but not that it has no intrinsic agency at all. There can only be a mauri of the forest, a physical objectification of the productivity of the forest, because the forest is (potentially) productive in itself, it is this ‘agency' which has been co-opted by the agency of the priests.

zh: 刚才描述的情形与模拟巫术之间的根本相似性，也许开始显现出来了：祭司制造并埋入森林的毛里（对象化的丰产力），既将森林原本具有的丰产力再现出来（事前），又成为森林后来丰产的原因（事后）。因为事前的丰产力能够被表现——即在一个索引中被对象化——它就落入了控制索引的人即祭司的掌控之中。换言之，祭司制造了一个森林生产力的索引，而这使森林具有生产力。他们得到猎人的酬报：猎人从森林那里获得其生产力的果实，再把它返还给祭司。可以说，这魔法必定灵验，因为促成丰产力的索引恰恰由它所促成的丰产力产生；这里存在一种完美却不可见的循环性。森林生产力的对象化与模拟巫术当然在一个本质方面有所不同：毛里把森林表现为繁茂兴旺，而巫术偶人则把巫术受害者表现为受伤甚至死亡。但机制是一样的：祭司通过把森林表现为繁茂而使森林繁茂；另一方面，同一种对象化若遭滥用，也可以用来伤害和杀死森林。事实上，如果敌人设法找到了森林的毛里，他们就会对着它念诵否定生产力的咒语，摧毁它的效力，给主人带来死亡，因为此刻这些毛里将对象化苦难，并造成苦难。这就相当于往巫术偶人身上扎针，以伤害那个被表现为受伤的受害者。
en: The fundamental similarity between the situation just described and volt sorcery will perhaps be beginning to show itself: the mauri (objectified fertility) created by the priests and buried in the forest is both a representation of the productivity of the forest (ex ante) and a cause of the forest being fertile (ex post). Because ex ante fertility can be represented—i.e. objectified in an index—it comes under the control of those who control the index, the priests. The priests, in other words, make an index of the productivity of the forest and that makes the forest productive. They are rewarded by the hunters, who receive from the forest the fruit of its productivity, and who return it to the priests. The magic, so to speak, just has to work, because the index of productivity is caused by the productivity it causes; there is a perfect, but invisible, circularity. The objectification of the productivity of the forest differs from volt sorcery, of course, in one essential respect, namely, that the mauri represents the forest as prosperous and flourishing, whereas the volt represents the sorcery victim as injured, or even dead. But the mechanics are the same; the priests make the forest flourish by representing it as flourishing; on the other hand, the very same objectification could be used to injure and kill the forest, were it subjected to abuse. In fact, if enemies managed to find the mauri of the forest, they would destroy its effectiveness by reciting productivity-negating chants over it, bringing death to the owners, for now these same mauri would objectify misery, and cause it. This is the equivalent of sticking pins into a volt to injure the victim represented as injured.

zh: 不过，在这方面最值得注意的是（Babadzan 1993: 61）：在毛里中被对象化的豪（丰产原理），同时也是用来指称巫师用来对受害者施术的蜕余物的词（引 Tregear 1891: 52）。我们现在明白为什么中空的毛里要放入“一绺绺头发”了。巴巴赞对巫术蜕余物与丰产原理之间的同义关系提出了一个最令人满意的解释：两者都涉及生长。蜕余物是身体上生长出来并分离出去的部分；这尤其适用于头发和剪下的指甲；的确，就成年人而言，这是人体所能提供的最明显的生长表现；即使头发不剪，它也仍会脱落、自行分离。蜕余物表现“生长”，因为它们可以说是不断地从活的身体上“收获”下来的。正如我们每次理发都是在收获我们的豪，猎人进入森林去“收获”那里的鸟时，他们收获的正是森林的蜕余物（豪）。
en: What is most interesting of all to note, though, in this connection (Babadzan 1993: 61) is that hau (fertility-principle) objectified in the mauri, is also the word used to refer to the exuviae used by a sorcerer to ensorcell his victim (citing Tregear 1891: 52). We now see why hollow mauri had ‘locks of hair' placed inside them. Babadzan suggests a most satisfactory explanation of the synonymy between sorcery exuviae and the principle of fertility: both involve growth. Exuviae are parts of the body which have grown and become separate; this particularly applies to hair and nail-clippings; indeed, where adults are concerned, these are the most obvious manifestations of growth that the human body provides; and even if hair remains uncut, it still falls out and separates itself. Exuviae represent ‘growth' because they are, so to speak, continually ‘harvested' from the living body. Just as we harvest our hau, whenever we have a haircut, so when the hunters enter the forest to ‘harvest' the birds there, they are harvesting the exuviae (hau) of the forest.

zh: 蜕余物巫术之所以可能，是因为身体在生长的同时会脱落其部分，而这些部分散布于周围环境之中。这里可以回想起一个惊人的呼应：卢克莱修把蛇与蝉蜕下的皮作为拟像或事物之“像”的典型实例；因为这些恰恰是由生长产生并散布四周的蜕余物。事实上，伊壁鸠鲁派理论把拟像的生成看作一个“生长”过程——万物在某种内在“推力”的作用下“脱落”短暂的表皮。
en: Exuviae sorcery is possible because of the fact that as the body grows, it sheds its parts, and these become distributed around the ambience. Here one may recall the remarkable resonance between Lucretius' instancing the skins shed by snakes and cicadas as prototypical simulacra or ‘idols'; for these are, precisely, exuviae produced by growth and distributed around. In fact, the Epicurean theory saw the generation of simulacra as a ‘growth' process-the ‘shedding' of ephemeral skins from all things induced by a kind of ‘pushing' from within.

zh: 毛里以丰产石而非人体蜕余物的面目出现时，它对象化了森林的生长，因为在概念上它就是那种生长所产出的东西；它是森林的蜕余物，落入祭司手中，被用于带来繁荣的“白”魔法，而非用来加害与招致歉收的黑魔法。
en: The mauri, in its guise as a fertility stone rather than as an item of human exuviae, objectifies the growth of the forest because it is, conceptually, something produced by that growth; it is the exuviae of the forest, which falls into the hands of the priests, who use it in the ‘white' magic of prosperity-induction rather than the black magic of sorcery and dearth-induction.

zh: 如我们所见，就物质形态而言，毛里丰产石可以采取多种形式。森林毛里是无像的，但用来促进甘薯生长的那些，则被雕刻成张着嘴的拟人形象，有时双手的姿势暗示着把食物放进嘴里。为保证人们有东西吃，这些形象本身也被做成正在进食的样子——当然它们自己也得到喂养，人们以初熟果实等祭品供奉它们。[
] 是巴巴赞为概括其总体论证所提供图示的一个版本。
en: Physically speaking, mauri fertility stones could take a variety of forms, as we have seen. Forest mauri were aniconic, but those used to promote the growth of sweet potatoes were carved as anthropomorphic images with open mouths, sometimes with their hands in a position suggesting the placing of food in the mouth. Ensuring that the people ate, they were shown eating-and they were of course fed themselves, with offerings of first-fruits and so on.
is a version of the figure Babadzan provides to summarize his general argument.

zh: 7.6　剥皮与索引的交换：塔希提的托奥
en: 7.6　Decortication and the Exchange of Indexes: Tahitian To’o

zh: 塔希提与毛利毛里石相当的物件也采取多种形式。渔业的生产力由一类称为普纳（puna）的提伊（ti'i；tiki＝“形象”）控制。这些“鱼”石像鱼一样呈长条形，某些实例上还刻有鱼鳃般的裂口。关于与普纳相关的仪式有一些描述，清楚表明其用法与毛里完全类似。巴巴赞令人信服地论证，用于农业的是另一类石头，雕有拟人特征，就像新西兰埋入甘薯田里的拟人毛里一样（同上，75–82）。这些生长石实际上被认为会生长，尽管极其缓慢。不幸的是，与塔希提农业仪式相关的文献存世不多，但可以肯定地说，那里曾施行与文献记载详尽得多的毛利仪式相当的增殖仪式（从民族史上看，毛利文明与语言渊源于社会群岛，其中塔希提最为重要）。也许最要紧的一点是：塔希提语词图普（tupu）基本义为“生长”，但也像豪一样指可用于巫术目的的蜕余物。换言之，图普就是塔希提语中与豪相当的词。
en: The Tahitian equivalent of the Maori mauri stone took a variety of forms also. The productivity of fisheries was controlled by a type of ti'i (tiki = ‘image') called Puna. These ‘fish' stones were elongated, like fish, and certain examples have fish-like gill slits on them. There are descriptions of the rituals associated with puna which make it clear that their use was entirely analogous to mauri. For agricultural purposes, Babadzan convincingly argues, a different type of stone was used, carved with anthropomorphic features, like the anthropomorphic mauri buried in sweet-potato fields in New Zealand (ibid. 75–82). These growth stones were actually believed to grow, though only very slowly. Not much documentation that is relevant to agricultural rites in Tahiti has unfortunately survived, but it is safe to say that increase-rituals comparable to the much better documented Maori ones were practised there (ethnohistorically, Maori civilization and language have antecedents in the Society Islands, of which Tahiti is the most important). Perhaps the most important point to bear in mind is that the Tahitian word tupu, which basically means ‘growth' also means, like hau, exuviae, usable for sorcery purposes. Tupu is the Tahitian equivalent of hau, in other words.

zh: 巴巴赞所讨论的塔希提材料的意义，并不在于单纯复制毛利农业仪式的模式以及豪、毛里等概念，更在于材料揭示了不同的社会与政治背景。毛利社会实际上自始至终是去中心化的，而古代塔希提却存在一个以奥罗崇拜为中心的国家雏形。因此，借助塔希提材料，我们仿佛能够从模拟巫术（私人事务）过渡到最庄严、最令人生畏的公共崇拜，涉及国神、即“权力之神”奥罗。
en: The interest of the Tahitian material discussed by Babadzan lies in a different direction than the mere replication of the Maori pattern of agricultural rites and the concepts of hau, mauri, etc. Maori society was effectively decentralized throughout, but in ancient Tahiti there was a proto-state with a centralized cult, the cult of Oro. Consequently, in relation to the Tahitian material, we are able, as it were, to pass from volt sorcery (a private affair) to public worship of the most majestic and awe-inspiring variety, involving the state god, the ‘god of power', Oro.

zh: 与用于农业和巫术的提伊形象（见

）——如鱼石和拟人雕刻——不同，奥罗崇拜以及较小神祇（重要亲属群体的祖先）崇拜的核心对象并非拟人的，尽管它们（在某种意义上）具有再现性，而且名称也不同。托奥（to'o）一词意为“支柱”、杖或柱。在神话中，托奥表现的是创世神所立、用以撑住天空的柱子，它保护奥（ao，光明与人类生命的世界）免受黑夜、黑暗与神性（波，po）的包围力量的侵蚀。托奥究竟应被视为再现性的（有像的）还是非再现性的（无像的），是一个悬而未决的问题。作为一端略粗于另一端的长条木料，它们可以被视为其名称所指的柱或支柱的“写实再现”。人们可以称它们为柱子的“有像”索引，因为它们指涉神话中撑天的柱子，而实际上并非那些柱子。另一方面，它们又以无像的方式表现具有拟人属性的神。奥罗本身并不是柱子。毋宁说，作为使天地分离——并由此连接天地——的柱子，托奥因与神毗连而获得神的临在，这里凭借的是相接的关系，而非形态相似。巴巴赞本人提出，托奥之所以无形，是因为神主宰一切有形之物的起源；作为赋予万物形式者，神自身无形。这一推论在塔希提创世吟唱中得到充分支持（Henry 1928；参见 Gell 1993: 124 ff.）。在这种情况下，托奥又是一种有像的形象——无形的形象，即无形性本身，或处于诞生状态（in statu nascendi）的万物。在我看来，有像再现与无像再现之间假定的对立在这里彻底瓦解了。托奥同时是完全有像的和完全无像的。不过，无可争辩的是：它们有原型，其原型就是神的人格。它们也像最卑微的巫术偶人一样，可被人操纵。通过它们，奥罗本人——塔希提宇宙中最强大的存在——能够经由再现而成为“被动施动者”，就像前例中的森林之豪，或模拟巫术中被动的受害者一样。
en: Unlike ti'i images (see

)-such as fish stones and anthropomorphic carvings, used in agriculture and sorcery—the objects at the centre of the Oro cult, and the cults of lesser gods, ancestors of important kin-groups, were not anthropomorphic, though they were (in a sense) representational, and they went by a different name, too. The word to’o means a ‘prop' or staff or pillar. The to’o represent, mythologically, the pillar placed by the creator god to hold up the sky and preserve the ao (the world of light and of human life) from the encompassing powers of night, darkness, and divinity (the po). It is a moot point whether the to’o deserve to be considered representational (iconic) or non-representational (aniconic). As elongated billets of wood, slightly thicker at one end than at the other, they might be regarded as ‘realistic representations' of pillars or props, which is what they are called. One could call them ‘iconic' indexes of pillars, in that they refer to the mythological pillars which hold up the sky without actually being these pillars. On the other hand, they represent, aniconically, gods who have anthropomorphic attributes. Oro was not a pillar, as such. Rather, as the pillar which keeps heaven and earth apart—and thus connects them—the to’o is invested with the god's presence by virtue of contiguity rather than resemblance. Babadzan himself suggests that the to'o is formless because the god presides over the origination of everything that possesses form; as the giver of forms to all things, the god is himself formless. This deduction is well supported in the Tahitian creation chants (Henry 1928; cf. Gell 1993: 124 ff.). In this case, the to’o is again an iconic image, a formless image or formlessness, or all things in statu nascendi. Here, it seems to me that the supposed contrast between iconic and aniconic representation comprehensively breaks down. The to’o are wholly iconic and wholly aniconic at the same time. What is quite inarguable though is that they have a prototype, and that their prototype is the person of the god. They are also, like the humblest volt, open to manipulation by human beings. Through them, Oro himself, the mightiest being in the Tahitian universe, could be rendered a ‘passive agent' via representation, just like the forest hau in the previous example, or the passive victim of volt sorcery.

zh: 沿着这一主题，我们能够发现，托奥所参与的首要仪式程序是一种剥皮仪式，即对神之蜕余物的受控生产。下面我将依据巴巴赞对现存文献的分析，描述这一仪式序列。
en: Pursuing this theme, we are able to discover that the primary ritual procedure in which the to’o were involved, was a ritual of decortication, of the controlled production of divine exuviae. Following Babadzan's analysis of the existing sources, I will now describe this ritual sequence.

zh: 首要的托奥是奥罗的化身。塔希提政治体系围绕对奥罗的马拉埃（marae，神庙）的控制权展开；谁控制了托奥，谁就控制了整个国家，敌对酋长们为此激烈争斗。重要的托奥可以说矗立于一个以神像为支柱的政体的顶端，而人类的社会等级与他们所掌管的托奥（以及等级更低的提伊、“巫术偶像”）的“等级”严格而精确地对应。社会等级与政治权力在一个称为帕伊阿图阿（pa'iatua）的仪式中得到定期而正式的表达，该词译意为“包裹诸神”（pa'i＝包裹、捆扎、束起）。（关于一般意义上的包裹，见 Gell 1993。）
en: The primary to’o were embodiments of Oro. The Tahitian political system revolved around asserting control over the marae (temples) of Oro; whoever controlled the to'o, controlled the country, and rival chiefs fought bitterly over them. The important to’o stood at the pinnacle, so to speak, of a polity of images, and social rank among human beings was strictly and precisely correlated with the ‘rank' of the to'o (and lower down the scale, ti'i, ‘sorcery idols') in their charge. Social rank and political power were given regular and formal expression at a ritual called pa'iatua, which, translated, means the ‘wrapping of the gods' (pa'i = wrap up, tie, bundle). (On wrapping in general see Gell 1993.)

zh: 只有在这一仪式中，托奥才示人观看，而且即便如此，也只向最重要、受仪式保护的祭司与酋长展示；地位较低的人一旦看见托奥就会立刻死去，因为它们充满了曼纳（塔希提语称这种品质为拉阿，ra'a）。为使它们不被看见，其余时间托奥都被紧紧包裹在编成的椰棕绳与塔帕树皮布制成的绑带中，有时外面还织上粗略勾勒的面部特征与四肢（
）。更重要的托奥则存放在专用容器中，以便贮藏与运输。帕伊阿图阿仪式的内容，是把一个地区的所有形象集合到马拉埃，更新它们的外层包裹，尤其是奥罗首要托奥的外层包裹。
en: Only during this ritual were to'o revealed to view, and even then, only to the most important and ritually protected priests and chiefs; the sight of a to'o would instantly result in the death of a lesser person, so filled were they with mana (a quality called raa in Tahitian). To protect them from view, to'o were at all other times tightly wrapped in bindings of sennit cordage and tapa bark-cloth, sometimes with roughly delineated facial features and limbs woven onto the outside (

). The more important ones were kept in special containers for storage and transport. The ritual of pa'iatua consisted of the assembly of all the images in a district at the marae, for the purpose of the renewal of their outer wrappings, especially the outer wrapping of the primary to'o of Oro.

zh: 我不必详述这一典礼。大体上，它是诸神列队进入马拉埃的仪式：主神领队（完全藏于其圣匣之中），地位较低的神按尊卑顺序跟随，随后是手持提伊即巫术形象而非托奥的“巫师”（他们同时护卫着队伍）（
）。埃利斯告诉我们（大英博物馆仅存的一件实例可资佐证），较小的神与提伊“巫术”形象并非无像的“柱”式，而是中空的拟人形象，体内有空腔，用以存放圣羽和／或巫术蜕余物（Ellis 1831: i. 339）。所有形象都按各自地位集合于马拉埃内外。在一处远离公众视线的独立圣所中，托奥被除去包裹、涂上油、摊放在阳光下。随后是一个重要的交换序列。
en: I need not describe the ceremony in any detail. Essentially, it consisted of a procession of the gods into the marae, led by the main god (completely hidden in its ark), with the lesser ones following in order of precedence, followed (and protected) by ‘sorcerers' bearing not to’o, but ti’i, sorcery images (

). Lesser gods and ti'i ‘sorcery' images, Ellis tells us (and there is a sole surviving example in the British Museum to back this up) were not in the aniconic ‘pillar' style, but were hollow anthropomorphic images, with an internal cavity for holding sacred feathers and/or sorcery exuviae (Ellis 1831: i. 339). All would assemble in and around the marae, according to their station. In a separate sanctuary, well away from public view, the to’o would be divested of their wrappings, oiled, and laid out in the sun. There then ensued an important exchange sequence.

zh: 塔希提政治权威最具象征意义的“通货”采取羽毛的形式，其中最重要的是红羽。佩戴红羽是最高酋长的服饰特权；马罗乌拉（maro ura，红羽腰带）标志着佩戴者居于最高酋长之位。不言而喻，羽毛是鸟的蜕余物，而鸟在整个波利尼西亚（正如在其他许多地方一样）都与天界相关联。红羽很可能也与血相关联——血是另一种蜕余物质，是生命、生长与繁殖力的索引。
奥罗尤其与羽毛和红色两者相关联。向奥罗致敬的首要行为是向他献上红羽，红羽或被织入裹在他身上的椰棕编绳，或用绳子系在上面，或干脆包在覆盖物里面。
en: The most symbolically significant ‘currency' of political authority in Tahiti took the form of the feathers, the most important being red ones. Wearing red feathers was a sumptuary privilege of the highest chiefs, the maro ura (red feather girdle) was synonymous with occupancy of the paramount chiefship. Feathers, needless to say, are the exuviae of birds, and birds have, everywhere in Polynesia (as so often elsewhere) heavenly associations. Red feathers are probably also associated with blood, another exuvial substance and index of life, growth, and reproductivity.

Oro was particularly associated with both feathers and redness. The primary act of homage to Oro was the presentation to him of red feathers, which would be woven into his sennit wrapping, attached to it by cords, or simply wrapped inside the covering.
