zh: 众人坐定后，大祭司打开圣匣，取出那令人敬畏的神像；当他在席子上将其揭开时，其他人也齐刷刷地揭开各自的神像……于是显露出来的低位诸神，包裹布折叠垫在身下，仍留在其主人手中，面向阿瓦阿（'ava'a），准备呈献给守护神［即奥罗］……当守护神的神像从其层层覆盖物上堆积如山的红黄羽毛中显露出来时……接着，小神的主人们按各自次序依次呈献小神，并献上新制的乌拉［红羽］护身符与散羽，经由大祭司转交给守护神，以换取守护神所拥有的羽毛［即刚从奥罗的椰绳包裹中解下的那些］。这一行为称为塔里托阿拉阿阿图阿（taritoara'a-atua，神的交换），据说能把给低位诸神增添来自大神的新力量。渔民的神最后呈献，因为它们来自海上。（Henry 1928: 166–7）
en: When all were seated, the high priest opened the ark and took out the dreaded image, and as he uncovered it upon the mat, the others all uncovered theirs in unison ... The minor gods then exposed, with their wrappers folded under them, remained in the hands of their owners, facing the 'ava'a ready for presentation to the tutelar god [i.e. Oro] ... When the image of the tutelar god was revealed from the profusion of red and yellow feathers lying upon its many coverings ... Then followed the presentation of the minor gods by their owners in their proper turns, with offerings of new ura [red feather] amulets and loose feathers, which were given through the high priest to the tutelar god in exchange for some in his possession [i.e. which had just been unwrapped from the sennit wrapper of Oro]. This act was called taritoara'a-atua (the god's exchange) and was supposed to add new power from the greater god to the lesser ones. The fishermen's gods were presented last because they were from the sea. (Henry 1928: 166--7)

zh: 巴巴赞给出了羽毛交换的如下图式：新的、未经圣化的羽毛从地位较低的祭司手中传到首要托奥（“主”奥罗）的祭司手中，而先前与首要托奥接触过的羽毛则传回给次级托奥。这样，首要托奥的一部分神圣性就分配给了集会中的次级托奥，以换取以新羽形式缴纳的贡赋——新羽可以说是一种“自然”产物，潜在地蕴含力量与丰产力，但尚不能产生它们。正如巴巴赞所指出的，只有与奥罗首要神像密切接触过一段时间的羽毛才具有这种生成属性（1993: 116）。羽毛必须与神同生共死——这是字面意义上的，因为看来要成为神的蜕余物，主神就必须“死去”，把蜕余物撒回世界。巴巴赞认为，这就是整个序列的意义所在，即先解开诸神的包裹、再把它们重新包起。解包把神带入世界，重新包裹则把神送回冥界波（po）。但由于神虽死去却留下了某物（他的羽毛、他的蜕余物图普），神的力量也被留了下来——留在酋长与奥罗祭司的手中。这一推论基于如下事实：塔希提高级酋长的丧葬仪式包括把尸体放在平台上晒干，然后包裹（捆扎）并以红羽装饰。这是为了控制强大的死者，使死者安稳地处于死亡状态，并因裹住他们的厚重树皮布绑带而无法伤害生者。这种处理（包裹并以羽毛装饰）只用于有权势的酋长的尸体和托奥，因此其含义是：在帕伊阿图阿仪式结束时，托奥正被当作一具“强大的尸体”对待。对托奥的捆扎把奥罗置于“受动者”的位置。
en: Babadzan provides the following schema of the feather exchange: new, nonsacred feathers passed from the lesser priests to the priests of the primary to’o (the ‘main' Oro) and the feathers which had previously been in contact with the primary to’o were passed back to the inferior to’o. In this way a portion of the sanctity of the primary to’o was distributed to the assembly of lesser to'o in exchange for a tribute paid in the form of new feathers, a ‘natural' product, as it were, potentially embodying power and fertility, but not yet able to generate it. Only feathers which, as Babadzan notes, had been intimately in contact with the primary image of Oro for some time, had this generative property (1993: 116). The feathers had to live and die with the god, quite literally, because it seems that to become divine exuviae, the primary god has to ‘die' and scatter exuviae back into the world. This, Babadzan thinks, is the significance of the sequence as a whole, that is to say the unwrapping of the gods followed by wrapping them up again. Unwrapping brings the god into the world, wrapping him up again sends the god back to the nether world, the po. But because the god has died but left something behind (his feathers, his exuviae tupu) the power of the god is also left behind-in the hands of the chiefs and the priests of Oro. This inference is based on the fact that the 'T'ahitian mortuary ritual for high chiefs involved the drying of the corpse in the sun, on a platform, followed by wrapping (binding) and decoration with red feathers. This was to keep the mighty dead under control, safely dead, and incapable, because of the massive bindings of bark-cloth enveloping them, from harming the living. Such treatment (wrapping and decoration with feathers) was reserved for corpses of powerful chiefs and for the to’o, so the implication is that the to’o, at the conclusion of the pa'iatua ceremony, is being treated as a ‘powerful corpse'. The binding up of the to’o places Oro in the ‘patient’ position.

zh: 以托奥形式进行的神崇拜及随之而来的羽毛交换，可以看作一种被极大放大了的模拟巫术操演。表面上，奥罗统治宇宙，但实际上他对人间事务的干预受酋长与祭司控制，途径是作为其部分、其蜕余物的索引，以及对其人格的首要索引——托奥——的捆扎。应当记得，古希腊巫师在代表受害者的小铅片上写下“我缚住，我缚住”的字样。在托奥崇拜中，我们发现这种对神的“束缚”真的被付诸行动，但含义相同。索引的原型借相似性被系于索引，从而受到控制。托奥本身被紧紧捆缚，其力量弥散进这些绑带，尤其是羽毛之中，羽毛于是成为政治控制的通货。
en: The cult of the gods in the form of to’o and the accompanying feather exchanges can be seen as a kind of vastly magnified exercise in volt sorcery. Ostensibly, Oro rules the universe, but in practice his intervention in human affairs is controlled by the chiefs and priests, via indexes which are his parts, his exuviae, and the binding of the primary index of his person, the to'o. It will be recalled that the ancient Greek sorcerers wrote on the little lead plates representing their victims, the words ‘I bind, I bind'. In the cult of the to’o we find this ‘binding' of the god literally enacted, but the implications are the same. The prototype of an index is bound to the index by resemblance, and is thus subjected to control. The to’o were themselves tightly bound, and their power diffused into these bindings, especially the feathers, which then became the currency of political control.

zh: 这一想法或许可以作更一般的表述，使之适用于一切宗教艺术。我们为上帝竖立的伟大纪念碑、宏伟的宗座圣殿与大教堂，都是索引，我们从中溯因推出上帝对世界、对其凡俗臣民的能动性；这些臣民为取悦他而奋斗劳作，身后留下这些巨大的外壳（或表皮），信众聚集其中，崇拜这一切辉煌的终极作者。无论如何，这就是关于宗教辉煌的正统观点，它把宗座圣殿与大教堂表现为献给全能上帝的“祭献”。然而，首先也必须承认：除非上帝的力量显现于此世的索引（行为的索引，或在当前情形下，物质的索引）之中，否则他根本算不上真正有力。那个基本的弥尔顿式悖论——上帝仅仅因为把自身分布于多种形态（包括撒旦）之中，就面临来自其造物的危险——以下述方式适用于这类关于上帝伟大的物质索引。人类对上帝享有一种留置权，因为他们掌握着上帝的对象化形式。即使上帝是以宏伟建筑与艺术品形式呈现的其相似性的终极作者，事实仍然是：在原因、工具与结果的序列中的某个关键点上，人类的能动性不可或缺。既然在此世，上帝的临在内在于这些人类能动性的作品之中，他就被绑缚于人类的目的——他那些表面上的仆人的此世繁荣与来世救赎——而非完全属于他自己的目的。他的能动性纠缠于我们的能动性之中，凭借的是我们制造（并成为）其拟像的能力。相对于我们的上帝，我们所处的位置，与毛利托洪加相对于森林之豪的位置完全相同。
en: This idea can perhaps be given a more general statement, so as to apply to all religious art. The great monuments that we have erected to God, the great basilicas and cathedrals, are indexes from which we abduct God's agency over the world, and over his mortal subjects, who have striven and laboured to please him, and have left these massive shells (or skins) in their wake, within which the faithful gather to worship the ultimate author of all this magnificence. Such, at any rate, is the orthodox view of religious magnificence, which represents basilicas and cathedrals as ‘offerings' to God, who is all-powerful. However, it must also be recognized, first of all, that God is not really powerful at all unless his power is apparent in this-worldly indexes (behavioural ones, or, in the present case, material ones). The basic Miltonic paradox that God is at risk from his own creation, simply by having distributed himself in manifold forms (including Satan), applies to such material indexes of God's greatness in the following way. Humanity has a lien on God because his objectification is in their hands. Even if God is the ultimate author of his resemblance in the form of magnificent structures and works of art, it remains the case that, at a critical point in the sequence of causes, instruments, and results, human agency is essential. Since, in this world, God's presence is inherent in these works of human agency, he is bound to human purposes, the this-worldly prosperity and other-worldly salvation of his ostensible servants, rather than to purposes entirely his own. His agency is enmeshed in ours, by virtue of our capacity to make (and be) his simulacrum. With respect to our god, we are in just the same position as the Maori tohunga with respect to the hau of the forest.

zh: 当然，我们把上帝困在其相似物之中这一事实，并不使一切宗教活动本身都成为巫术。在宗座圣殿中向上帝致敬并非破坏性或恶意的，但它确实使上帝成为本质上属人的意图的“被动施动者”，正如向托奥致敬使奥罗成为酋长与大祭司的被动施动者。我毫不怀疑，基督教神学家要反驳这种指摘毫无困难，其方式至少能令他们自己信服，但在我看来，这一情境的逻辑无可逃避。教皇头衔“最高祭司”（Pontifex Maximus；JVLIVS II PONTIFEX MAXIMVS 赫然题写在罗马圣彼得大教堂的使徒像上方）赋予教皇在大地与天空之间架桥的权力。教皇在天地之间的“桥”与塔希提托奥——使天地分离（但也保持交通）的杖或支柱——之间的类比，似乎太过惊人，不容不加评论。而在圣彼得大教堂，人们确实可以察觉一个明确的含义：上帝是他那些更重要的臣民（如尤利乌斯二世）的交换伙伴，即便不是他那些地位卑微的广大崇拜者的交换伙伴。圣彼得大教堂就是那座桥；但要点在于，桥的建造被明确无误地归于教皇尤利乌斯二世及其前任与后任。用交换的术语说，他是首要赠予者，是基图姆（kitoum）即“不受他人权利约束的贵重物”（Munn；见下文第9.3节）的持有者——它被派出去寻找其匹配物，即能够与之衡量并作为回礼送回来的贵重物。圣彼得大教堂作为礼物—对象与人类能动性的索引，引出一个回应性的回礼；悖谬的是，这回礼就是圣彼得大教堂本身，它被赋予了如今可供人类使用的神圣力量，就像献给奥罗的羽毛作为他的化身从奥罗那里返回一样。
en: Of course, the fact that we have trapped God inside his likenesses does not make all religious activity sorcery, as such. The homage paid to God in the basilica is not destructive or malignant, but it does make him the ‘passive agent' of essentially human designs, just as the homage paid to the to’o made Oro the passive agent of the chiefs and high priests. I have no doubt that Christian theologians would have no difficulty in refuting such an imputation in a manner convincing, at least, to themselves, but the logic of the situation seems to me inescapable. The papal title ‘Pontifex Maximus' (JVLIVS II PONTIFEX MAXIMVS blazoned over the apostle of St Peter's in Rome) attributes to the Pope the power to build bridges between earth and heaven. The analogy between the papal ‘bridge' between earth and heaven, and the Tahitian to'o-the staff or prop which keeps heaven and earth apart (but also in communication)-seems too remarkable to pass without comment. And in St Peter's one can certainly detect the clear implication that God is the exchange-partner of his more important subjects such as Julius II if not the mass of his worshippers of low estate. St Peter's is the bridge; but the point is that the making of the bridge has been attributed unambiguously to the Pope, Julius II, his predecessors and successors. He, in exchange terms, is the primary donor, the holder of the kitoum, the ‘unencumbered valuable' (Munn; see below, Sect. 9.3) which is sent out to find its match, the valuable which can be measured against it and returned for it. St Peter's, as a gift-object and an index of human agency, elicits a responsive counter-gift, which, paradoxically, is St Peter's itself, invested with divine power now available to mankind, like the feathers which, given to Oro, return from Oro as his embodiments.

zh: 不过，我们不必在这类类比上耽搁太久，它们可能被认为缺乏说服力，甚至令人反感。现在我要转向拟人形象的崇拜——托奥与圣彼得大教堂都不能算在其中，至少乍看之下不能。

关于偶像崇拜的文献总体上对这一实践深乏同情；几乎可以说，学会读写就使人丧失了满怀热情地从事这一实践的资格。这倒支持了这样一种观念：有文字社会的思维模式（本质上不倚赖感官）与文字出现之前的思维模式（感性的、参与式的）之间存在一道“大分水岭”。然而，近年来已出现对“大分水岭”理论的反拨（Parry 1985），当今世界上确实存在大量识字的形象崇拜者，也有古老的有文字文明把向图像致敬置于宗教实践的核心，印度教就是其中一例。认为只有未受教育者或“原始人”才崇拜仿照人形制成的石、木、金属偶像，这一观念是反形象宗教性形式（如犹太教、伊斯兰教及某些基督教宗派主义与新教形式）与一种更普遍、且有古代渊源的宗教怀疑论的兴起相互汇合的结果。的确，凡有宗教之处，很可能也有怀疑论，无论是否公开表达。人类学家确实在文盲与未受教育者中遇到过无数对仪式效力持怀疑态度的例子，因此这不能仅仅归因于识字或“科学”的兴起。
en: However, let us not delay too long over such analogies, which may be regarded as unconvincing, or even offensive. I now want to turn to the worship of anthropomorphic images, among which neither the to’o nor St Peter's may be counted, at least, not at first glance.

The literature of idol-worship is, in the main, profoundly unsympathetic to this practice; it is almost as if learning to read and write disqualifies one from engaging in this practice with any enthusiasm. This rather supports the notion that there is a ‘great divide' between the essentially non-sensuous mode of literate thinking and the sensuous, participatory mode of pre-literate thinking. However, there has been a reaction against the theory of the ‘great divide' in recent years (Parry 1985) and there certainly exist numerous literate image-worshippers in the world today, and ancient, literate, civilizations whose religious practices centre on the paying of homage to images, such as Hinduism. The idea that only the uneducated or ‘primitive' worship idols of stone, wood, and metal fashioned to resemble the human form, is a consequence of the convergence between anti-imagistic forms of religiosity (such as Judaism, Islam, and certain forms of Christian sectarianism and Protestantism) and the rise of a more generalized religious scepticism, which has ancient antecedents. Indeed, wherever religion exists, it is probable that scepticism also exists, whether or not this is expressed in public. Certainly, anthropologists have encountered innumerable examples of scepticism concerning the efficacy of rites among the illiterate and uneducated, so this cannot be attributed to literacy or the rise of ‘science' alone.

zh: 7.7　达显：作为能动性的见证
en: 7.7　Darshan: Witnessing as Agency

zh: 信仰与怀疑的文化基础问题不必在此纠缠，但对西方人和无信仰者来说，要设身处地理解偶像崇拜者仍然极其困难，因为我们从意识到这类事情的那一刻起，就经受着反偶像崇拜宣传的狂轰滥炸。也许最能启发洞见的形象崇拜论述出自印度教文献，因为这一宗教的信徒在向形象表达虔敬时最不避讳。戴安娜·埃克（Diana Eck, 1985）为印度形象崇拜的浩繁文献提供了一个便捷的导论。崇拜形象就是从神那里获得达显（darshan）——一种经由眼睛传达的特殊祝福。达显是神赐予信徒的，是神在世间行使能动性的一种方式，而崇拜者是受动者（用我们的图式说，即接受者-P）。活人也能像神一样给予达显；古鲁（guru）在弟子集会上现身时就在给予达显（见 Babb 1987），重要政治人物出现在支持者集会上时也是如此——支持者前来，既为聆听，也为目睹其领袖。达显是上位者给予下位者的礼物或供奉，其内容是“显现之礼”，被想象为某种祝福的物质性传递。
en: Questions of the cultural foundations of belief and scepticism need not detain us, but it is still enormously difficult for Westerners and non-believers to empathize with idol-worshippers because of the bombardment with antiidolatrous propaganda which we have experienced from the very moment we became conscious of such things. Perhaps the most insight-provoking accounts of image-worship belong to the literature of Hinduism, because followers of this religion are among the least self-conscious in showing devotion to images. A convenient introduction to the copious literature on image-worship in India has been provided by Diana Eck (1985). Worshipping images is obtaining darshan from the god, a particular type of blessing conveyed through the eyes. Darshan is something given by the god, a mode of the god's agency in the world, and the worshipper is a patient (the Recipient-P, in terms of our scheme). Living human beings can give darshan, as well as gods; a guru gives darshan when he or she makes an appearance before a gathering of disciples (see Babb 1987), and the same is true of an important politician appearing before an assembly of supporters, who have come to see, as much as to hear, their leader. Darshan is a gift or an offering, made by the superior to the inferior, and it consists of the ‘gift of appearance' imagined as a material transfer of some blessing.

zh: 在我看来，达显与印度分配神圣祝福／人格的另一种模式本质上相似：即分发圣食普拉萨德（prasad），由神的虔信者食用（当然，基督教中也有类似做法）。普拉萨德常被概念化为神的“食物残余”（jutha），其方式与巫术所用的蜕余物完全类似。据埃克说，达显的概念化与印度教传统赋予眼睛作为人际交流器官的角色密切相关。
en: It seems to me that darshan is essentially similar to the other mode in which divine blessing/personhood is distributed in India: the distribution of sacred food, prasad, which is consumed by the god's devotees (of course, there are Christian parallels to this as well). Prasad is often conceptualized as the ‘food leavings' (jutha) of the god, in a manner absolutely analogous to the exuviae used in sorcery. According to Eck, the conceptualization of darshan is closely allied to the role allotted in the Hindu tradition to the eye as an organ of interpersonal transactions.

zh: 因此，作为神之能动性模式的达显，与邪眼观念密切相关。神圣的偶像、宗教古鲁与声名显赫的政治家，以稳定而穿透的目光辐照他们所主持的集会，借此传递祝福。可以说，这是邪眼巫术的积极的“白”的一面；较为不完美的存在者则通过卑劣、嫉妒、恶意的目光传递邪眼巫术。因此，置身于神的偶像之前，就是向神的目光敞开自身，并把神的形象内化。
en: Darshan, considered as a mode of divine agency is thus intimately connected to the concept of the evil eye. Divine idols, religious gurus, and politicians of renown transfer blessings via the steady and penetrating gaze with which they irradiate the assembly over which they preside. This is, so to speak, the positive ‘white' aspect of evil-eye sorcery, which more imperfect beings transfer via their mean, envious, and ill-intentioned looks. To place oneself before the idol of the god, therefore, is to lay oneself open to the divine gaze and to internalize the divine image.

zh: 不过，这只是从一个角度考察问题；即使在印度，崇拜神也需要崇拜者方面的意志行为，崇拜者相对于被崇拜者也是施动者。（作为受动者）从神那里接受达显，取决于接受者发起的“取”（darshan lena）这一有明确对象的行动。埃克引用了斯特拉·克拉姆里施对“看”的论述，她将看理解为能够作用于对象的一种能动性：
en: This is to examine the question from only one angle though; even in India, it takes an act of will on the part of the worshipper to worship the god, and the worshipper is also an agent with respect to the one being worshipped. The reception (as a patient) of darshan from the god is contingent on the transitive action of ‘taking' (darshan lena) initiated by the recipient. Eck cites Stella Kramrisch's account of ‘seeing' as transitive form of agency:

zh: 看……是目光向对象伸展。目光触及对象并获得其形态。触摸是最终的联结，可见之物凭这一联结而变得可以把握。当眼睛触摸对象时，其中搏动的生命力便被传达……（Kramrisch 1976: 136）
en: Seeing ... is a going forth of the sight towards the object. Sight touches it and acquires its form. Touch is the ultimate connection by which the visible yields to being grasped. While the eye touches the object the vitality that pulsates in it is communicated . . . (Kramrisch 1976: 136)

zh: 克拉姆里施的这些评论得益于她对梵文哲学著作的了解。古印度哲学家持有与柏拉图主义者类似的观点：视觉是一种“外射的”感官，眼睛通过空气发出不可见的光束或射线，在可见对象的表面触及它们。一位哲学家遮罗迦（Caraka）论证说，我们其实只有一种感官，即触觉，视觉、听觉等不过是其更精细的形式（Sinha 1934）。其他哲学家不同意，但共识仍然是：看与触摸一样，是一种接触形式。相比之下，伊壁鸠鲁的理论（见上文）是“内摄的”；影像（eidola）从对象流溢出来，进入眼睛。但卢克莱修表明，即便如此，伊壁鸠鲁派仍把看等同于触摸。这些像轻如薄纱，却是物质性的。内摄说把接触的位置放在眼睛表面，外射说则让眼睛发出的光束接触物体表面。我不认为伊壁鸠鲁派借事物之“像”解释视觉的内摄理论在印度有对应物，因此不能把形象崇拜的盛行归因于它的影响。但另一种外射理论如果说有什么区别的话，反而更具解释力，因为它在“看”（达显）与触摸、涂油等其他同形象的物质互动形式之间建立了直接联系。这些触觉性的致敬形式是印度教形象崇拜中非常重要的要素。
en: These remarks of Kramrisch are informed by her knowledge of Sanskrit philosophical writings. Ancient Indian philosophers held views similar to those of the Platonists, that sight was an ‘extromissive' sense, the eye sending out invisible beams or rays through the air, which touched the objects of sight at their surfaces. One philosopher, Caraka, argued that indeed we only have one sense, the sense of touch, of which sight, hearing, etc. are just more subtle forms (Sinha 1934). Other philosophers disagreed, but the consensus was none the less that seeing was, like touching, a form of contact. Epicurus' theory (see above), by contrast, is ‘intromissive'; the eidola emanate from the object and enter the eye. But Lucretius shows that seeing was, even so, equated with touching by the Epicureans. The (gossamer, but physical) idols were touched at the surface of the eye, not at their own surfaces, via the eye-beams. I do not think that the Epicurean intromissive theory of vision by ‘idols' had an Indian counterpart, so one could not attribute the prevalence of image-worship to its influence. But the alternative extromissive theory is, if anything, even more explanatory, because it forges a direct link between ‘seeing' (darshan) and other types of physical interaction with the image, such as touching, anointing, and so on. These tactile forms of homage are very important elements in Hindu image-worship.

zh: 某些印度哲学家（Sinha 1934）把看类比为盲人用棍杖探明外物形状。这种唯物主义的视觉观反映在克拉姆里施关于达显的论述中：看在一个存在者与另一个存在者之间架起一座物质桥梁。希尔恩的基本洞见——就“形象”而言，“相似”与“接触”之间其实没有区别——在这里被完全揭示出来，无需援引伊壁鸠鲁的类比。
en: Certain Indian philosophers (Sinha 1934) made the analogy between seeing and the use of a stick by the blind, in order to ascertain the shape of external objects. This materialistic conception of seeing is reflected in Kramrisch's statement about darshan; seeing creates a physical bridge between one being and another. Hirn's basic insight that in relation to ‘images' there really is no distinction between ‘similarity' and ‘contact' is fully brought into the open here, without the need to invoke the Epicurean parallel.

zh: 因此，达显在很大程度上是双向的事情。神投向崇拜者的目光赐予祝福；反过来，崇拜者也凭目光向神伸展，触及神。其结果是与神合一，依虔信者的解释，即意识的融合。这重新引出了形象（索引）与接受者之间关系中的互惠性与主体间性问题。人与索引之间——尤其是像神像这样具有人形的索引——应当可能存在主体间性，这一点显然与这几章所论证的总论点密切相关。不可否认，从崇拜神像的虔信者的观点看，神像是一个社会性他者的显现，神—虔信者关系是一种社会关系，完全可以与虔信者同另一个人之间的关系相比。然而，仅仅把这当作一个民族志的、描述性的事实接受下来，而不去更深地追问这一关系的认知基础，未免太容易了。尽管虔信者宣称并真诚相信，有死的虔信者与不死的神性之间达成了心智的合一，虔信者毕竟也生活在一个普通对象的世界里，那些东西只是物，没有被赋予主体性，在这个世界里，拥有类人意识与能动性的人与无生命的“物”之间的区别很容易划定。虔信者确实知道神像只是形象，并非血肉之躯；如果形象碰巧动了、说话了、或似乎在喝牛奶，那是奇迹，是因其出乎意料而引人注目的事件。这类显现会增强虔敬，但人们也承认，神只有在人们对诸神的信仰跌至低谷、需要非常事件来支撑时，才肯赐予奇迹。真正的虔敬理想上无需这类或任何别的奇迹即可达成。
en: Darshan is thus very much of a two-way affair. The gaze directed by the god towards the worshipper confers his blessing; conversely, the worshipper reaches out and touches the god. The result is union with the god, a merging of consciousnesses according to the devotionalist interpretation. This brings back the issue of reciprocity and intersubjectivity in the relationship between the image (the index) and the recipient. It is clearly germane to the general thesis argued in these chapters that intersubjectivity between persons and indexes, particularly indexes which, like images of the gods, are human in form, should be possible. It cannot be denied that, from the point of view of the devotees worshipping the image of the god, the image of the god is a manifestation of a social Other, and that the god devotee relationship is a social one, absolutely comparable to the relationship between the devotee and another human person. However, it is too easy just to accept this as an ethnographic, descriptive, fact, without a deeper questioning of the cognitive basis of this relationship. For all that the devotee asserts, and truly believes, that a union of minds is achieved between mortal devotee and immortal divinity, the devotee none the less also lives in a world of ordinary objects, mere things devoid of imputed subjectivity, in which the distinction between human beings-possessed of human-being-like consciousness and agency and inert ‘things' is readily drawn. The devotee does know that the image of the god is only an image, not made of flesh and blood; and if, perchance, the image moves, or speaks, or seems to drink milk, that is a miracle, a remarkable occurrence because so unexpected. Devotion is enhanced by such manifestations, but it is admitted that the gods only vouchsafe miracles when faith in them has reached a low ebb, and needs to be buttressed by extraordinary happenings. True devotion is attainable, ideally, without miracles of this or any other kind.

zh: 偶像的生命性与被赋予的主体性，唯有克服无生命形象与活的存在者之间的鲜明差异才能获得。这是如何发生的？
en: The animacy and imputed subjectivity of the idol is not attained except by surmounting the stark difference between an inert image and a living being. How does this happen?

zh: 就印度教材料而言，赋灵过程的关键似乎至少起初取决于看与被看的逻辑。形象虔敬是一种视觉行为（与祈祷等相对），完全由看来完成。具体说，它由注视神的眼睛来完成；合一来自目光接触，而不是对形象可能呈现的所有其他细节的端详——那些细节标明神的身份与属性，增添整体效果，却并非虔敬所必需。凝视虔信者的神的眼睛，映照着凝视神的虔信者的行动。有时（如在耆那教神庙中），形象的眼睛镶着小镜子，使虔信者在观看时能看见自己映在形象眼中。即使没有实际的镜子，就其眼部活动而言，形象也映照着虔信者的行动（
en: So far as the Hindu material is concerned, the key to the process of animation seems, initially at least, to depend on the logic of looking and being seen. Imagistic devotion is a visual act (as opposed to prayer, etc.) and it is accomplished entirely by looking. Specifically, it is accomplished by looking into the eyes of the god; union comes from eye contact, not the study of all the other details the image may show, which indicate the identity and attributes of the god and which add to the general effect without being devotionally essential. The eyes of the god, which gaze at the devotee, mirror the action of the devotee, who gazes at the god. Sometimes (as in Jain temples) the eyes of images are set with little mirrors, so that the devotee can see himself or herself reflected in the image's eye in the act of looking. Even in the absence of actual mirrors, the image, so far as its ocular activity goes, reflects the action of the devotee (

zh: 生命性起源于这种目光的交互，因为即使一个人对形象不持神秘主义态度，他也仍然有权把“看”（或“微笑”“做手势”等）这样的行动动词用于形象。一个彻底的怀疑论者可以说——事实上不得不说——偶像“看”着某个特定方向；这话不会引起注意，因为人人都接受：偶像“看”的标准就是它的眼睛睁着并朝向某个特定方向。问题是：偶像看的时候看见了什么？虔信者看见的是偶像正在看他或她，它正用目光回望信徒，映照着信徒自己的动作。导致“形象‘看见’虔信者”这一实践推论的，并不是虔信者方面的神秘主义，因为我们从来只能通过知道别人在看什么来知道他们看见了什么。怀疑论者会说“偶像是瞎的——它什么也看不见”，但即便如此，盲就是无法看见自己所看的东西，这几乎谈不上驱除了形象残留的生命性，因为缺陷蕴含着潜在的能力。而虔信者无需作出这一推论，事实上也无法作出，因为情境是按虔信者自己的能动性及其结果来定义的：虔信者看，并且看见。作为镜子的形象在做虔信者所做的事，因此形象也看，并且看见。要断言形象能看见，甚至在逻辑上也不必把“生命”赋予形象；毕竟，人们常说照相机“看见”东西，却并不暗示照相机有生命。
en: Animacy takes its origin from this ocular exchange, because, even if one does not take a mystical attitude towards images, one is none the less entitled to apply action verbs like ‘look' (or ‘smile', ‘gesticulate', etc.) to them. A perfect sceptic can say, in fact is obliged to say, that an idol ‘looks' in a particular direction; the remark would pass unnoticed because everybody accepts that the criterion for idols ‘looking' is that their eyes should be open and pointed in a particular direction. The question is, what do idols see when they look? What the devotee sees is the idol looking at him or her, performing an act of looking, mirroring his or her own. It is not mysticism on the devotee's part which results in the practical inference that the image ‘sees' the devotee, because we only ever know what other persons are seeing by knowing what they are looking at. The sceptic would say ‘the idol is blind-it cannot see anything', but even so, to be blind is to be unable to see what one looks at, which hardly banishes the residual animacy of images, since a disability implies a potential ability. And the devotee need not draw this inference, in fact, cannot, because the situation is defined in terms of the devotee's own agency and result; the devotee looks and sees. The image-as-mirror is doing what the devotee is doing, therefore, the image also looks and sees. One does not even logically have to impute ‘life' to an image to assert that an image can see; after all, people often speak of cameras as ‘seeing' things, without implying that cameras have life.

zh: 但“偶像既然能看，就能看见”这一推论并未被明确作出；如果明确作出，就可能招致怀疑论的反驳。镜像效应还有一个后果，使这一推论不会直接面对这种质疑。这就是看与被看所形成的逻辑回溯。目光接触、相互注视，是主体间性的基本机制，因为注视他人的眼睛不只是看见他人，而是看见他人正在看见你（我看见你看见我看见你看见我，如此等等）。目光接触引发一种自我意识：自己在他人眼中是什么样子；此时，人“从外部”看自己，仿佛自己也是一个对象（或一尊偶像）。目光接触似乎提供了通达他人心智的直接途径，因为主体从作为主体的他人的观点出发，把自己看作一个对象。目光接触是“二阶意向性”——把他人（人）意识为意向主体——的基本模式。因此，在形象崇拜中，虔信者不只是看见偶像，而是看见自己（作为对象）正被偶像（作为主体）看见。虔信者把自己觉察为偶像视线所及的对象，偶像的“看见”由此隔了一层被纳入她的自我意识。她看见自己如偶像看她那样：跪在偶像面前，仰首凝视。既然她能看见自己正在看偶像，偶像就必定看见她，因为当她看见自己正在看偶像时（从她的观点看，这是她直接经验到的事实），偶像是被她看见正在看她的。“偶像看见她”是“她看见自己正在看偶像”的一个嵌套成分。这种回归使虔信者与偶像的视角以这种方式在逻辑上相互咬合，其净结果是一种光学振荡：偶像与虔信者的视角来回切换，速度如此之快，以致人际边界被抹去，“合一”得以达成。这种经由目光接触的相互包摄，以
示意。下文（第7.12节）讨论形象的开光程序时，我将回到“眼睛”在偶像崇拜中的重要作用。
en: But the inference that if idols can look, they can see, is not drawn explicitly; if it were, it might be open to sceptical objections. It is protected from judgement by a further consequence of the mirror-effect. This is the logical regression set up by seeing and being seen. Eye-contact, mutual looking, is a basic mechanism for intersubjectivity because to look into another's eyes is not just to see the other, but to see the other seeing you (I see you see me see you see me etc.). Eye-contact prompts self-awareness of how one appears to the other, at which point one sees oneself ‘from the outside' as if one were, oneself, an object (or an idol). Eye-contact seems to give direct access to other minds because the subject sees herself as an object, from the point of view of the other as a subject. Eye-contact is the basic modality of ‘second-order intentionality', awareness of the other (person) as an intentional subject. Thus, in imageworship, the devotee does not just see the idol, but sees herself (as an object) being seen by the idol (as a subject). The idol's ‘seeing' is built into the devotee's own self-awareness at one remove as the object which is seen by the idol. She sees herself as the idol sees her, kneeling before it, gazing upwards. In that she can see herself seeing the idol, the idol must see her, because when she sees herself seeing the idol (from her point of view, a datum of immediate experience) the idol is seen by her as seeing her. The ‘idol seeing her' is a nested component of ‘her seeing herself seeing the idol'. The net result of the regression whereby devotee's and idol's perspectives become logically interdigitated with one another in this way is a kind of optical oscillation in which idol's and devotee's perspectives shift back and forth with such rapidity that interpersonal boundaries are effaced and ‘union' is achieved.
