zh: 阿阿特别值得注意之处，是这个“单一”神性的形象以明确的方式把神性表现为（字面意义上的）小人之间关系的集合。由此，阿阿消除了一与多、内与外的对立。这个形象的表面由若干相互融合的自身复制品构成，或者说由一系列出芽的凸起构成。在内部，这个形象由它自身按更小尺度在其内腔中的复制构成。因此，它既形象化了人格作为外部关系总和的观念（谱系的结果，在时空中展开），同时又形象化了人格源于拥有一个内在之人、一个小人——或在此例中，一群小人——的观念。我们不能像通常把人的边界等同于其身体的空间边界那样把阿阿个体化，因为阿阿没有这样的边界；它像俄罗斯套娃，在这方面，它不可抗拒地令人想起《培尔·金特》中的诗句，主人公把（道德和生命史意义上的）人比作一个洋葱，由一系列同心层构成：
en: What is particularly remarkable about the A'a is the explicit way in which this image of a ‘singular' divinity represents divinity as an assemblage of relations between (literally) homunculi. In so doing, the A'a obviates the contrast between one and many, and also between inner and outer. The surface of this image consists of amalgamated replications of itself, or alternatively, a succession of budding protuberances. Internally, the image consists of itself, replicated on a smaller scale, within its own interior cavity. As such, it images both the notion of personhood as the aggregate of external relations (the outcome of genealogy, fanning out in time and space) and at the same time the notion of personhood as the possession of an interior person, a homunculus, or, in this instance, an assemblage of homunculi. We cannot individuate the A'a in the way in which we normally individuate persons by identifying the boundaries of their person with the spatial boundaries of their bodies, for the A'a has no such boundaries; it is like a Russian doll, and in this respect, it irresistibly recalls the lines in Peer Gynt in which the hero compares the (moral, biographical) person to an onion, composed of a succession of concentric layers:

children: ——哼，你不过是个洋葱——
现在，我的好培尔，我要把你一层层剥开，
眼泪和哀求都帮不了你。
［拿起一个洋葱，一层层剥皮］
剥下这破破烂烂的外皮——
那是翻船后趴在舢板龙骨上的落难人。
这一层是乘客——瘦骨伶仃，
可还带着一点培尔·金特的味道。
再往下是淘金的自我——
汁液嘛，要是有过，也早没了。
这层粗皮，带着硬茧，
是哈得孙湾设陷阱捕皮毛兽的猎人。
二话不说，扔掉。
接下来是考古学家，矮小却有活力；
这儿是先知，水灵新鲜——
照俗话说，一股谎话的臭味，
能叫诚实的人辣出眼泪。
这层皮卷曲，带着女人气，
是过着享乐生活的绅士。
下一层看着病恹恹，带着黑纹——
黑色可以指牧师，也可以指黑鬼……
［他一下子剥掉好几层。］
层数多得难以置信！
咱们就不能快点剥到芯吗？
［他把整个洋葱撕碎。］
不，见鬼，剥不到。一直到中心
什么都没有，只有层——越来越小的层……
大自然真会开玩笑！
—Why, you're simply an onion—
and now, my good Peter, I'm going to peel you
and tears and entreaties won't help in the least.
[Taking an onion, he strips it skin by skin]
There goes the battered outer layer—
that's the shipwrecked man on the dinghy's keel.
This layer's the passenger—scrawny and thin,
But still with a bit of a taste of Peer Gynt.
Next underneath comes the gold-mining Self—
the juice, if it ever had any is gone.
This rough skin here, with the hardened patch
is the fur-trapping hunter from Hudson's Bay.
We'll throw that away without a word.
Next the archaeologist, short but vigorous;
and here's the prophet, juicy and fresh—
it stinks of lies, as the saying goes,
and would bring tears to an honest man's eyes.
This skin, curled and effeminate,
is the gentleman living his life of pleasure.
The next looks unhealthy and streaked with black—
black could mean either priests or niggers . . .
[He peels off several layers at once.]
What an incredible number of layers!
Don't we get to the heart of it soon?
[He pulls the whole onion to pieces.]
No, I'm damned if we do. Right down to the centre
there's nothing but layers—smaller and smaller . . .
Nature is witty!

zh: 培尔·金特的洋葱也是一个分形，与阿阿具有同样本质上的同心形式。易卜生使用这一意象的用意，是表明培尔·金特的人格没有终极基础；他由一层层累积起来的生命史（关系）经验构成，但他仍必须独自为此负责。从陷于十九世纪唯物主义与个人主义困境的培尔·金特，到赋形于阿阿的神学冲动，两者或许相距不远。在阿阿身上，造物主是以世界为身体的心智。它显现为一个身体，由其他身体组成，层层递归，无穷无尽。
en: Peer Gynt's onion is also a fractal, of the same essentially concentric form as the A'a. Ibsen's idea, in utilizing this image is to show that there is no ultimate basis to Peer Gynt's personhood; he is made of layers of biographical (relational) experience accreted together, for which none the less, he must take sole responsibility. Perhaps it is not such a vast step to pass from Peer Gynt trapped in the aporias of nineteenth-century materialism and individualism to the theological impulse which motivates the A'a, which depicts the divine creator, the mind of which the world is the body, in the form of a body composed of other bodies, ad infinitum.

zh: 这一观念在玛丽琳·斯特拉森（1988；参见 Gell 1998）与罗伊·瓦格纳（1991）等作者关于美拉尼西亚人格的研究中得到了当代表达。尤其是瓦格纳发展了“分形人格”概念，用以克服典型的“西方”对立：个体（自我）与社会、部分与整体、单数与复数。谱系观念在我们的两个波利尼西亚例子（当然都是偶像）中得到了显著表达，它是使多成为一、使一成为多的关键意象。任何个体的人都是“多重的”，意思是个体是众多谱系关系凝结而成的，每一种关系都在这个人身上体现；反过来，人的集合体——如宗族或部落——由于是一个谱系而是“一个人”：始祖如今体现为许多身体，都是从他的一个身体转化而来的。瓦格纳写道：
en: This idea is given contemporary expression in the work on personhood in Melanesia, by writers such as Marilyn Strathern (1988; cf. Gell 1998) and Roy Wagner (1991). Wagner, in particular, has developed the notion of ‘Fractal Personhood', which he mobilizes to overcome the typically ‘Western' oppositions between individual (ego) and society, parts and wholes, singular and plural. The notion of genealogy, which is so signally expressed in our two Polynesian examples (both idols, of course), is the key trope for making plurality singular and singularity plural. Any individual person is ‘multiple' in the sense of being the precipitate of a multitude of genealogical relationships, each of which is instantiated in his/her person; and conversely, an aggregate of persons, such as a lineage or tribe, is ‘one person' in consequence of being one genealogy: the original ancestor is now instantiated, not as one body but as the many bodies into which his one body has transformed itself. Wagner writes:

zh: 分形的人既不能被看成与集合体发生关系的单位，也不能被看成与单位发生关系的集合体。分形的人始终是一个实体，关系内在于其中。也许内在关系最具体的例证来自一般化的生殖与谱系观念。从生殖来看，人作为另一个人的一部分，由那人“孕育”。一个人也能“孕育”或产生他人，成为这些人谱系上或生殖上的“因子”。因此谱系是人串成的链条，正如在加速放映的人类生活影片中，可以看到人从彼此身上“出芽”。作为人类个体的人与作为宗族或氏族的人，同样是对这条链的任意切分或认定，是其分形性的不同投影。但借身体的生殖而形成的链条，也只是内在关系的一种具体形式。人们使用共同的语言，也是这种关系的表现。（1991: 163）
en: A fractal person is never a unit standing in relation to an aggregate, or an aggregate standing in relation to a unit, but always an entity with relationship integrally implied. Perhaps the most concrete illustration of integral relationship comes from the generalised notion of reproduction and genealogy. People exist reproductively by being ‘carried' as part of another, and ‘carry' or engender others by making themselves genealogical or reproductive ‘factors' of these others. A genealogy is thus an enchainment of people, as indeed persons would be seen to ‘bud' out of one another in a speeded-up cinematic depiction of human life. Person as human being and person as lineage or clan are equally arbitrary sectionings or identifications of this enchainment, different projections of its fractality. But then enchainment through bodily reproduction is itself merely one of a number of instantiations of integral relationship, which is also manifest, for instance, in the commonality of shared language. (1991: 163)

zh: 从人类学的观点看——即便不是从哲学的观点看——源于嵌入社会环境的外在能动性观与源于内在主观自我的“内在主义”能动性理论之间的冲突，其解决要到这种“成链关系”中去寻找，即内在自我（关系性的）与外在自我（同样关系性的，但尺度更大）之间的结构同构。斯特拉森的著作（1988）尤其探讨的“谱系心智理论”，似乎在阿阿的形式中得到了完美表达。
en: From the anthropological point of view, if not the philosophical one, the solution to the conflict between the external notion of agency, deriving from insertion in the social milieu, and the ‘internalist' theory of agency, deriving from an inner subjective self, is to be sought in this ‘enchainment', the structural congruence between the inner self (which is relational) and the outer self (which is equally relational, but on an expanded scale). The ‘genealogical theory of mind' which is explored, particularly, in Strathern's work (1988) seems perfectly expressed in the form of the A'a.

zh: 但这件艺术品及波利尼西亚的同类作品并非孤例。事实上，供祭祀崇拜使用的雕塑往往有一个“具有意义的内部”，雕像的功能也远超单纯的再现。像阿阿那样可以打开、露出其他形象的雕塑形象，在古希腊就有制造，并为阿尔喀比亚德提供了形容其导师苏格拉底的比喻（柏拉图在《会饮》213–15中叙述）：
en: But this artwork, and its Polynesian cousins, is not unique. In fact, the possession of ‘significant interiors' is a very common feature of sculptural works specifically intended for cult use, rather than as mere representations. Sculptural images which open up, like the A'a, to reveal other images, were manufactured in ancient Greece, and provided Alcibiades with a simile for his mentor, Socrates (as narrated by Plato in the Symposium 213-15):

zh: 各位，我在此要赞美苏格拉底，我就用比喻来赞。哦，是的，他也许以为这只是开玩笑，但我拿它作比是为了说出实情。那么我说，他活像西勒诺斯——就是你们在雕塑匠的店里看到的小像；匠人制作它们，它们拿着排箫或笛子，可以从中间打开或向后翻开，然后就露出里面的神像。我还要说，他像萨提尔玛尔叙阿斯［被阿波罗剥皮的那位］……
en: I am here to speak in praise of Socrates, Gentlemen, and I will just do it by means of similes. Oh yes, he will perhaps think it is only for a bit of fun, but my simile will be for truth, not for fun. I say then, that he is exactly like a Silenos, the little figures that you see in statuaries' shops; the craftsmen make them, they hold panpipes or pipes, and they can be opened up down the middle or folded back, and then they show inside them, images of the gods. And I say further, that he is like Marsyas the Satyr [who was flayed by Apollo] ...

zh: 这里的对比是苏格拉底丑陋的外表（身体）与神圣的内部（心智）。同一种形象也在基督教崇拜艺术中发展出来，尽管神学含义不同。中世纪制作过一类称为“开合圣母”（vierges ouvrantes）的圣像，但存世极少，也许因为这类形象特别容易助长偶像崇拜，如下面卡米尔《哥特式偶像》中的一段所示。“博尔顿圣母”在宗教改革前曾立于达勒姆大教堂的一座小堂，它是：
en: Here the contrast is between the ugly exterior (body) and the divine interior (mind) of Socrates. The same kind of image was also developed in Christian cult art, though with a different theological implication. A class of holy statues called ‘vierges ouvrantes' was made in the Middle Ages, though few have survived into the present, perhaps because these images were particularly conducive to idolatry, as the following passage from Camille's work of The Gothic Idol shows. ‘Our Lady of Bolton' which used, before the Reformation, to stand in a chapel of Durham cathedral was:

zh: 一尊奇妙、栩栩如生而美丽的圣母像，称为博尔顿圣母，像身自胸部以下装有铰链，可作两扇打开。像内雕绘着救主之像，镀金极精，双手举起，两手之间持一尊美丽硕大的纯金基督十字苦像；每逢耶稣受难日，此十字像被请出，当日凡在该教堂者皆匍匐趋前。每逢重大节日，该像开启，使众人得见像内所绘圣父、圣子、圣灵，工艺极精，镀金极美。（Camille 1989: 230–1）
en: a marveylous lyvely and bewtifull Image of the picture of our Ladie, so calld Lady of Boultone, which picture was made to open with gymmers [or two leaves] from her breasts downwards. And within this saide immage was wroughte and pictured the immage of our Saviour, merveylouse fynlie gilted holdynge uppe his hands, and holding betwixt his hands a fair large Crucifix of Christ, all of gold, the which Crucifix was to be taken fourthe every Good Fridaie, and every man did creepe unto it that was in that Church at that daye. And every principall daie the said image was opened, that every man might see pictured within her the Father, Son and the Holy Ghost, most curiouslye and fynely gilted. (Camille 1989: 230-1)

zh: 卡米尔图示了这类“开合圣母”的一个德国实例（
）。“博尔顿圣母”与更常见的圣髑盒形式的基督教圣像类型相关，因为她除了是圣母像之外，又用来收存耶稣受难日巡游时展示的金十字苦像。（“开合圣母”的印度对应物参见

：猴神哈奴曼敞开胸膛，露出罗摩与悉多。）这类形象即使在普遍使用之时也备受争议：卡米尔引用神学家热尔松1402年的话，谴责“加尔默罗会”形象“腹中有三位一体，仿佛整个三位一体都在童贞玛利亚身上取了肉身……”（1989: 232）。这些形象太有生命了，它们透着召魂巫术的意味。在同一本书后面，卡米尔展示了装有圣徒遗骨的头形圣髑匣如何成为官方深深猜疑的对象，尤其是据说圣殿骑士团在异教仪式中崇拜的银制和金制的头形圣髑匣——骑士团因此在1308年被镇压（同上，271–7）。据传由罗吉尔·培根发明的臭名昭著的“会说话的头”是同一主题的另一变体（同上，246–7）。但宗教艺术与巫术的关系极深，我们已经看到了。
en: Camille illustrates a German example of such a ‘vierge ouvrante' (

). ‘Our Lady of Bolton' was related to the more common type of Christian holy image in the form of a reliquary, in that she was, besides an image of the Virgin, a container for the golden crucifix which was paraded on Good Friday. (For an Indian parallel to a ‘vierge ouvrante' cf.

showing Hanuman, the monkey god, opening his breast to reveal Rama and Sita.) Such images were controversial even when they were still in common use: Camille quotes the theologian Gerson, in 1402, denouncing ‘Carmelite' images which ‘have the Trinity in their abdomen as if the entire Trinity assumed flesh in the Virgin Mary . . .' (1989: 232). These images were all too animate, they smacked of necromancy rather than religion. Later on in the same book, Camille shows how reliquary heads, containing the bones of saints, could become objects of deep official suspicion, especially the silver and golden heads supposedly worshipped in pagan ceremonies by the Knights Templars, who were suppressed in 1308 as a result (ibid. 271-7). The notorious ‘talking head' reputedly devised by Roger Bacon is another variation on the same theme (ibid. 246-7). But the relation between religious art and sorcery runs very deep, we have already seen.

zh: 更普通的人形圣髑匣没有这样的恶名，其中有许多著名实例，如弗里德伯格图示并讨论的那些（1989: 92–5，图30–2）。这位作者还指出，中世纪的教堂除非安放了圣髑，否则根本无法祝圣。正如圣髑赋予圣髑匣雕像以生命，使它成为特别神圣的对象（内部有心智——或更准确地说，有灵——的对象），教堂建筑作为一个整体也成为一个“身体”，其赋灵同样需要置入圣髑。把圣髑置入教堂建筑的常规位置是祭坛背饰内部、祭坛本身之中，或埋在祭坛之下。
en: No such opprobrium attached to more ordinary reliquaries in human form, of which there are many famous examples, such as those illustrated and discussed by Freedberg (1989: 92-5, figs. 30-2). This author also remarks on the fact that in the Middle Ages, churches could not be consecrated at all unless they had holy relics installed in them. Just as relics animated the reliquary image, rendering it a particularly holy object (an object with a mind, or perhaps more precisely, a spirit, within it) so the church (fabric) as a whole became a ‘body' whose animation also required the insertion of a relic. The normal place for the insertion of relics into the fabric of a church was inside the altarpiece, in the altar itself, or buried beneath it.

zh: 不过，把赋灵的圣髑置入形象引出了一个新的问题，即怎样为神像行祝圣仪式，让“单纯”的人造物变成力量的载体，能有意地行事，也能回应信众的意图。我们将在下一节考察偶像崇拜的这一方面。
en: The insertion of animating relics into images raises a fresh question, however, that of consecration-the management of the transition between the religious image as a ‘mere' manufactured thing and a vehicle of power, capable of acting intentionally and responding to the intentions of devotees. We shall consider this aspect of idolatry in the next section.

zh: 7.12　祝圣仪式
en: 7.12　The Rites of Consecration

zh: 可以说，当今形象或偶像崇拜最盛行的地方是南亚，在印度教徒中间，以及（实行上有所不同）在佛教徒中间。在那里，形象仍在大量制作并安奉于圣地，人类学家得以细致观察开光仪式。因此，本节将围绕三个著名的南亚实例展开论证：普里贾甘纳特偶像的开光（Eschmann et al. 1978），理查德·贡布里希（1966）对僧伽罗寺院中佛像安奉的记述，以及迈克尔·艾伦（1976）对加德满都塔莱珠女神（杜尔迦）“活神像”开光的记述。
en: It is fair to say that the worship of images or idols is most extensively practised, nowadays, in south Asia, among Hindus and (in a rather more qualified way) among Buddhists. Here images are still being produced and installed in holy places in great numbers and here it is possible for anthropologists to observe the rites of consecration in detail. I shall therefore conduct the argument of this section with reference to three well-known south Asian examples, the consecration of the idol of Jagganath in Puri (Eschmann et al. 1978), the account given by Richard Gombrich (1966) of the installation of a statue of the Buddha in a Sinhalese monastery, and finally, the account given by Michael Allen (1976) of the consecration of the ‘living image' of the goddess Taleju (Durga) in Kathmandu.

zh: 普里（奥里萨）神庙中的贾甘纳特及其兄弟巴拉巴德拉、苏巴德拉与其妻苏达尔沙纳的神像，位列全印度最受尊崇的偶像。然而，尽管它们是拟人像，一眼就看得出来它们是截下的圆柱形树干，经过装扮，添上初具轮廓的上肢和硕大无比的眼睛。就物质而言，这些神像并不古老，尽管其样式确实古老，因为它们必须每十二年、至多每十九年在名为纳瓦卡莱瓦拉（navakalevara）的仪式上更换一次。埃施曼关于普里贾甘纳特崇拜的历史及其与“部落”宗教之亲缘关系的著作中，收录了对这一仪式的详细描述（G·C·特里帕蒂撰写）。这一重要印度教崇拜与部落的亲缘关系毋庸置疑；我本人曾在印度同一地区（巴斯塔尔县，东邻奥里萨高地）的部落民穆里亚冈德人中做田野，他们的神像是不具四肢与眼睛的无像木柱，但在其他方面与贾甘纳特神像极为相似，只是尺寸较小（A. Gell 1978；参见 S. Gell 1992）。
en: The images of Jagganath, his brothers, Balabadhra and Subadhra, and his wife Sudarsana in the temple of Puri (Orissa) are among the most revered idols in the whole of India, but, though anthropomorphic, these images are (visually speaking) quite obviously cylindrical sections of tree-trunk, dressed up and equipped with vestigial upper limbs and very, very, large eyes. The images are not old in physical terms, though their design is indeed ancient, since they have to be renewed every twelve, or at most every nineteen years, in the course of a ceremony called navakalevara. A detailed description of this ceremony (contributed by G. C. Tripathi) is provided in Eschmann's work on the history and affinities in ‘tribal' religion of the Puri Jagganath cult. The tribal affinities of this important Hindu cult are not in doubt; I myself worked in the same region of India (Bastar district, which abuts onto the Orissa highlands to the west) among tribal Muria Gonds, whose images of divinities were aniconic wooden posts, without limbs or eyes, but otherwise highly resembling the Jagganath images, though on a reduced scale (A. Gell 1978; cf. S. Gell 1992).

zh: 特里帕蒂对纳瓦卡莱瓦拉的记述是一流的民族志描述，遗憾的是我无法在此详细概述。这一更新仪式分为五个阶段，如下：
en: Tripathi's account of navakalevara is a first-rate exercise in ethnographic description, which I cannot unfortunately summarize in any detail. The ceremony of renewal has five phases, as follows:

zh: 1. 寻得具备规定特征的达鲁（daru，圣木）并将其运至神庙（包括在伐树前献祭以驱避恶灵等，并为树祝圣）；
en: 1. To find out the daru (sacred wood) with the prescribed characteristics and to bring it to the temple (involving a sacrifice to ward of evil spirits etc. and to sanctify the tree before felling it);

zh: 2. 雕刻神像的木质结构；
en: 2. The carving of the wooden structure of the images;

zh: 3. 将“生命物质”（brahmapadartha）置入神像，为之开光；
en: 3. The consecration of the images by the insertion of the ‘life-substance' (brahmapadartha) into them;

zh: 4. 埋葬旧像，以及代塔人（Daitas，低种姓的庙役）的葬礼与净礼；
en: 4. The burial of the old figures, the funeral and purificatory rites of the Daitas (temple servitors, of low caste);

zh: 5. 以数层布等覆盖物并施彩绘，赋予神像最终形态（Eschmann 1978: 230）。
en: 5. Giving the images their final form by means of several coverings of cloth etc. and by applying paint to them (Eschmann 1978: 230).

zh: 我略去这一过程的前两个阶段，只提一点：神像的效力最初取决于达鲁树的吉祥位置与形态（它必须长在水边，四周有三座山环绕，树皮深色、呈“红”色，树干笔直，有四根枝条，等等）。达鲁树的砍伐、运输与木工制作伴随着众多仪式。神像由低种姓但享有高仪式特权的庙役代塔人制作，他们是前部落民，唯有他们懂得按精确规则制作这类木像，其工作的重要方面甚至对婆罗门祭司也保密。他们最重要的秘密之一，就是神像“生命物质”（brahmapadartha）的真实性质。
en: I omit the first two phases in this process, except to mention that the efficacy of the images depends, initially, on the auspicious location and form of the daru tree (it must grow by water, be surrounded by three mountains, have dark, ‘red' bark, a straight trunk, with four branches, etc.). Numerous ceremonies accompany the felling, transport, and carpentering of the daru tree. The images are made by temple servitors of low caste but high ritual privilege, the Daitas, ex-tribals who alone know how to create this type of wooden image, according to precise rules, important aspects of their work being kept secret by them, even from the Brahmin priests. Among the most important of their secrets is the actual nature of the ‘life-substance' (brahmapadartha) of the images.

zh: 开光程序与神像雕刻同时开始，最初由婆罗门主持。由于神像尚在制作中，婆罗门便致力于对另一块达鲁木开光，这块木头分成四块后，将成为成品神像上容纳“生命物质”的腔穴的“盖”。这块木头先以献给恶灵的供品加以保护，再经繁复的沐浴与净化，然后安放在仪式用床上休息。此后，数日之内，通过对木头每一部分（与身体各部分对应）诵念真言，将那罗辛哈神（贾甘纳特既是其一种形态，也是克里希纳的一种形态）之灵引入木中。这一召请程序称为尼亚萨达鲁（nyasadaru）。此后，经仪式处理的达鲁木——通过转喻，这也适用于此刻正在代塔人工坊中作为神像完工的那些更大的达鲁木段——在灵性意义上被赋予了生命、血肉、感官等等。然后便可将其切成四块盖板，装入四尊神像。
en: The consecration procedure commences simultaneously with the carving of the images, and is first of all conducted by Brahmins. Since the images are still being made, the Brahmins devote their efforts to consecrating a separate piece of daru wood, which, divided into four pieces, will become the ‘lids' over the cavities in the finished images containing their ‘life-substance'. This piece of wood is protected with offerings to evil spirits, then elaborately bathed and purified, then placed to rest on a ritual bed. After this, the spirit of the god Narasimha (of which Jagganath is a form, as well as being a form of Krishna) is induced into the wood by the recitation of mantras on each of its parts (equated with the parts of a body) over a number of days. This invocation procedure is called nyasadaru. After this, the ritually treated daru wood-and by metonymy, the larger sections of daru wood which are at this moment reaching completion as images in the Daitas workshop-is spiritually speaking endowed with life, flesh, blood, sense organs, etc. It can then be cut into four lid-pieces to fit into the four images.

zh: 然而，关键仪式不由婆罗门而由代塔人执行。他们从神庙取出“旧”像，剥去层层浸树脂的绑布。这样就能打开旧像内藏“生命物质”的隔腔。
en: The crucial ceremony however, is not conducted by the Brahmins but by the Daitas. These take the ‘old' images from the temple, and strip from them the many layers of resin-impregnated cloth with which they are bound. They can then reach the compartments inside the old images in which their ‘lifesubstance' is secreted.

zh: 受命执行此任务的代塔人在深夜打开旧像的腹部，双眼蒙住，双手包裹至肘，使他既看不见也摸不到神像的生命物质。装有生命物质的匣子随后从旧穆尔提［神像］中取出，放入新像。新像的腔穴随即以尼亚萨达鲁［圣木］四块之一覆盖，这块圣木已由婆罗门开光约两周。（特里帕蒂，载 Eschmann 1978: 260）
en: The Daita entrusted with the job opens the belly of the old image in dead of night with his eyes blindfolded and the hands wrapped up to the elbows so that he may neither see nor feel the brahmapadartha of the image. The casket containing the Brahmapadartha is then taken out of the old murti [image] and placed in the new one. The cavity of the new image is then covered with one of the four pieces of the Nyasdaru [sacred wood] which has been consecrated for about two weeks by the Brahmins. (Tripathi in Eschmann 1978: 260)

zh: 除了代塔人，没有人确切知道生命物质究竟由什么物体或物质构成。它可能是一件遗物，据说卡拉帕哈达在1568年率穆斯林毁像者焚烧一尊贾甘纳特木像，遗物便是那件木像烧剩下的一截。在婆罗门看来，它是一块萨拉格拉玛（salagrama），一种圣石，通常是来自喜马拉雅山的椭圆形河卵石，内含菊石化石和／或孔洞（见
，采自 Mookerjee and Khanna 1977）。
en: Nobody really knows, except the Daitas, exactly of what object or substance the brahmapadartha is composed. It may be a relic, a portion of a wooden Jagganath supposedly incinerated (but not completely) by the Muslim iconoclasts under Kala Pahada in 1568. In the opinion of the Brahmins, it is a salagrama, a type of sacred stone, usually an oval river-pebble from the Himalayas containing fossilized ammonites, and/or cavities (see
from Mookerjee and Khanna 1977).

zh: 代塔人随即为失去生命物质的已故神像举行葬礼。他们哭泣哀悼，遵守为期十天的丧礼中有关不洁的禁忌。不过他们也从中获益：他们获准保留旧像的绑布，剪成布条卖给朝圣者。这些布条为购买者带来护佑与好运。
en: The Daitas now perform burial rites over the deceased images which have lost their life-substance. They weep and mourn, observing mortuary pollution restrictions for ten days. However, they derive benefit from this, in that they are allowed to keep the cloth wrappings of the old images, which they cut into strips and sell to pilgrims. These pieces of cloth confer protection and good fortune on the purchasers.

zh: 开光的最后阶段现在到来。属于另一种姓的庙役——据说是卡亚斯塔（Kayasthas，婆罗门的一种低等形式）——承担包裹神像的工作：木质的神像只是“骨架”，要用它们的“肉”，即布与颜料来包裹。木质“骨骼”先以樟脑油浸渍来“洗浴”，这给骨头以“骨髓”。然后，据说要用长长的红线缠绕它们，代表“血管”。此后，再裹上许多浸过树脂（血）与淀粉（脂肪、精液）的红布条（肉），直到神像开始呈现最终形态。最外层的包裹就是神像的皮肤。
en: The final phase of consecration now occurs. Another caste of temple servants, said to be Kayasthas (a low form of Brahmins) undertake the wrapping of the images -who, in wooden form are just ‘skeletons'-with their ‘flesh', that is, with cloth and paint. The wooden ‘bones' are first of all ‘washed' by being impregnated with camphor oil. This gives the bones ‘marrow'. Then, apparently, long red threads are wound around them, representing ‘blood vessels'. After this, many strips of red cloth (for flesh) impregnated with resin (blood) and starch (fat, semen) are added, till the image begins to assume its final form. The outer wrappings are the image's skin.

zh: 最后，由精通此艺的画师（chitakara）为神像施彩。使新像开光最终完成的最后一个动作，是点画神像巨眼中的瞳仁，由婆罗门祭司亲自执行，同时诵念吠陀真言。给神像眼睛点上最后一笔之后，婆罗门为每尊像沐浴，以洗去神像先前与低种姓木匠、画师等接触所沾染的污染。这不是直接给神像沐浴，而是给神像的“像”沐浴——即为此专门保存的大铜镜中映出的影像。此后，新像在盛大的仪仗与典礼中被巡行展示，安奉在神庙中它们原有的位置（特里帕蒂，同上书：262–4）。
en: Finally, the images are painted by craftsmen skilled in this art (chitakara). The very last act, which finalizes the consecration of the new images, is the painting in of the pupils of the immense eyes of the images, which is done by the Brahmin priests themselves, reciting Vedic mantras the while. After giving the last stroke of paint to the eyes of the images, the Brahmins give each a bath, to remove the pollution from the previous contact the images have had with low-caste carpenters, painters, etc. This is done not by bathing the image directly, but bathing the images' images, cast in large bronze mirrors kept for this purpose. After this, the new images are paraded and installed in their place in the temple with great pomp and ceremony (Tripathi, ibid. 262-4).

zh: 这些有趣的仪式中有两个方面与我们特别相关。神像的开光显然同时按两条平行策略进行：首先是代塔人的策略，着重把生命物质放入神像内部的腔穴；其次是婆罗门的策略，方向相反，通过以赋予生命的真言向那块代替神像受祝的木头呼告（尼亚萨达鲁阶段），以及为神像眼睛的瞳仁点上最后一笔。换言之，代塔人的程序可称为由内而外的程序，婆罗门的程序则是由外而内的程序。两者都不可或缺，互为补充。
en: Two aspects of these interesting ceremonies are of particular concern to us. The consecration of the images evidently proceeds according to two parallel strategies simultaneously; first of all, the strategy of the Daitas, which focuses particularly on the placing of the life-substance inside the image, in the cavity, and secondly, the strategy of the Brahmins, which proceeds in the inverse direction, through the apostrophization of the representative billet of wood with life-endowing mantras (the phase of nyasadaru) and the application of the final stroke of paint to the pupils of the images' eyes. In other words, the Daitas' procedure could be called the inside-out procedure, while the Brahmins' procedure is the outside-in procedure. Both are necessary and mutually complementary.

zh: 代塔人的程序或许更为原始，因为它试图在拥有“灵魂”与拥有一个住着小人（homunculus）的内腔之间建立物理类比。此外，它是“谱系性的”，因为它通过“代”与“代”神像之间的物质传递，在旧像与新像之间建立了亲属纽带。婆罗门的策略大体上比这更抽象：他们不是塑造神像，而是以真言向它致辞，借“言辞的魔力”（Tambiah 1985）从外部赋予它生命。我们不难看出，这两种策略恰好对应先前在心智与能动性哲学中辨识出的两条路线。代塔人的策略是“内在主义”的，婆罗门的策略是“外在主义”的。但若以为这两种策略相互独立，那就错了。归根结底，婆罗门也向内在主义策略让步，因为他们的最终动作是对神像的物理改变，而不仅仅是呼告。他们为神像眼睛点瞳仁的收官之举是既是摹仿，也通过形似起作用。尽管这些神像的眼睛实际上并不透明，但任何眼睛的瞳仁都从来不是“物”，而总是孔洞、孔口，通往“心智”所居的隐秘内部。偶像的表面不是不可穿透的屏障，而是通达这个至关重要的内部的途径。
en: The Daitas' procedure, is, perhaps, the more primitive, in that it seeks to render a physical analogy between the possession of a ‘soul' and the possession of an interior cavity inhabited by a homunculus. Moreover, it is ‘genealogical' because it establishes a kinship link between the old images and the new ones through the transmission of substance between ‘generations' of images. The Brahmin strategy, for the most part, is more abstract than this; rather than fashion the image, they address it with mantras, animating it externally through ‘the magical power of words' (Tambiah 1985). We can easily see that these two strategies correspond exactly to the two strands previously identified in the philosophy of mind and agency. The Daitas' strategy is the 'internalist' one, the Brahmins' the 'externalist' one. But it would be false to suppose that these two strategies are independent. In the end, the Brahmins concede to the internalist strategy to the extent that their final act is one of physical modification of the image, not mere apostrophization. Their culminating act of painting in the pupils of the eyes of the image is mimetic and iconic. Though the eyes of these images are not actually transparent, the pupils of any eyes are never 'things' but always holes, orifices, giving access to the hidden interior within which 'mind' resides. The surface of an idol is not an impermeable barrier, but a means of access to this essential interior.

zh: 事实上，贾甘纳特及其同伴的神像就是一系列“皮”，恰如培尔·金特的洋葱，其意涵也相同：终极的中心永远无法抵达。偶像在这里与偶像有关的最外层皮由普里神庙本身构成（它当然是一个小宇宙），其中充满神圣的言辞与气味——言语之皮与嗅觉之皮（参见 Anzieu 1989: 59）。偶像居于这个回荡的小宇宙的中心并赋予它生命，同时又被神圣言辞的不息之流赋予生命。向中心行进，我们经由一层“社会之皮”接近偶像：那是朝圣者、随侍庙役与祭司的人群，他们以关注与虔敬让身处芸芸众生聚会中心的偶像有了生命。偶像本身供奉于中心，以祭坛为框，饰以大簇鲜花和珠宝，坐拥面前堆积如山的供品——那是它们以财产形式呈现的外皮。我们无法接近或触摸偶像，因此向中心的旅程只能在想象中继续。我们看到的是它们可见的皮，但那只是外层包裹。这些包裹由众多层次构成，其内皮是肉、脂肪、精液、血、骨、骨髓。我们可以逐一穿透它们，或者凝视偶像的巨眼，直接进入它们的身体。但那墨黑的水潭之下、之后藏着什么？里面有一个原初的腔穴，一层内皮。腔穴之内，有某种能赋予生命的东西。从概念上我们知道，这个腔穴里其实放着一只匣子，又一层内中之皮。匣子里是什么？也许连放它进去的人也不知道；他肯定从未见过里面的东西。我们相信那里有一块萨拉格拉玛，一块圣石或世界种子。若是如此，萨拉格拉玛里面又是什么？萨拉格拉玛本身也有内部，有通往这内部的孔洞（参见
）。我们必须进入这些孔洞。然后我们会发现什么？谁能说得清——这要紧吗？——因为至此已经清楚：神像的赋灵根本不是一个找到“神圣中心”的问题。要紧的只是皮的不断重复，向外朝向大宇宙，向内朝向小宇宙，以及这些皮的结构彼此对应这一事实；没有确定的“表面”，没有确定的“内部”，只有永不停息的出出入入，而赋灵之谜正是在这往返出入之中得到解答。
en: In fact, the images of Jagganath and his companions are a series of ‘skins' just like Peer Gynt's onion, with the same implication that the ultimate centre can never be reached. The outermost (relevant) skin of the idols consists of the temple of Puri itself (which is, of course, a microcosmos) which is filled with sacred words and odours-verbal and olfactory skins (cf. Anzieu 1989: 59). The idols reside in the centre of, and animate, this reverberating microcosmos, and are animated by the incessant flow of sacred words. Proceeding towards the centre we approach the idols through a ‘social skin', the throng of pilgrims and attendant temple servants and priests, who, by their attentions and devotions, animate the idols occupying the cynosure of a great assembly of souls. The idols themselves are enshrined at the centre, framed on their altars, adorned with masses of flowers and jewellery, presiding over their material wealth of heaped-up offerings, their external skins in the form of possessions. We cannot approach or touch the idols, so we can proceed further on our journey towards the centre in imagination only. What we see are their visible skins, but these are only outer wrappings. These wrappings consist of numerous layers, their inner skins of flesh, fat, semen, blood, bone, marrow. These we may penetrate, one by one, or gazing into the enormous eyes of the idols, we can enter their bodies directly. But what is there, concealed beneath, behind, the inky pools? Inside, there is a primordial cavity, an internal skin. And inside the cavity, an animating presence of some kind. Conceptually, we know that, in fact, this cavity contains a casket, another inner-inner skin. And what is in the casket? Even the man who placed it there does not know perhaps; he has certainly never seen its contents. We believe that there is a salagrama there, a sacred stone or world-seed. If so, what is in the salagrama? The salagrama itself has an interior, and, holes leading into this interior (cf.

). We must enter these holes. And then what would we find? Who can say-and does it matter? -for by now it is apparent that the animation of the image is not a matter of finding the ‘sacred centre' at all. What matters is only the reduplication of skins, outwards towards the macrocosm and inwards towards the microcosm, and the fact that all these skins are structurally homologous; there is no definitive ‘surface', there is no definitive ‘inside', but only a ceaseless passage in and out, and that it is here, in this traffic to and fro, that the mystery of animation is solved.

zh: 贡布里希（1966；参见 Freedberg 1989: 84–7, 95 的讨论）描述的斯里兰卡佛像开光遵循类似的模式，只是有所简化。佛教徒，尤其是僧侣，本不应崇拜偶像，但通过供奉与礼敬的姿势向佛像表示尊敬，是获取功德、确保较好的来世的一种方式，尽管不算特别重要。再一次证明：佛像若要具有任何宗教重要性，也必须是藏纳舍利之所。少许佛陀的舍利被置入像内，使之有效力。然而按贡布里希的说法，这并不构成开光；开光由画师完成，他在一场名为内特拉·平卡马（netra pinkama，“眼睛仪式”）的特殊仪式中为佛像点画眼睛（1966: 25）。
en: The consecration of an image of the Buddha in Sri Lanka, described by Gombrich (1966; cf. the discussion in Freedberg 1989: 84-7, 95) follows a similar pattern, though reduced. Buddhists, especially monks, are not supposed to worship idols, but showing respect to images of the Buddha, by making offerings and gestures of submission, is one way to acquire merit and secure a good rebirth, if not a very significant one. Once again, it proves to be the case that images of the Buddha are, if they are to have any religious importance, also reliquaries. Minute portions of the Buddha's bodily remains are placed inside images to render them efficacious. However, this does not consecrate them, according to Gombrich; consecration is accomplished by the craftsman, who paints in the eyes of the image in the course of a special ceremony called netra pinkama the ‘eye ceremony' (1966: 25).

zh: 这一仪式与贾甘纳特神像的开光相比，既有有趣的对照，也有许多延续之处。婆罗门／代塔人的关系在僧伽罗佛教的开光仪式中，双方的分工有一部分正好调了过来。在普里，是代塔人把“生命物质”放入神像使之赋灵，由婆罗门祭司点画眼睛；而在斯里兰卡，是僧侣（住持）把舍利放入佛像，由在家画师点画眼睛。这精确反映了佛陀（一个具有超乎凡人的道德品格的已故之人）与印度教诸神（非人的不朽者）之间的差异。佛像颂扬的是“善终”的可能性，僧侣则是半死之人，志在达到善终的终极境界。因此，处理佛陀舍利——遗体的一部分——理当交给自身半死的僧侣；在斯里兰卡（或泰国；参见 Tambiah 1985）这样的佛教国家，他们当然总是主持葬礼（但不主持诞生仪式和婚礼）。于是，从某种意义上说，舍利所做的，是通过置入“死亡物质”使佛像变得“死”，从而像佛陀——这里“成佛意味着活着便已进入死亡”的说法颇为悖谬。然而可以看出，这一仪式程序几乎谈不上神像的“赋灵”。贡布里希把这理解为使佛像作为佛陀形象获得“正当性”的手段，这样从僧侣的视角看就不沾偶像崇拜的污点。对在家信众则不然。对他们来说，佛陀确实是一位神。礼拜者深陷世俗生活及其罪孽，走近佛像，透过它的眼睛感到佛陀活生生地在场，希望与佛陀相通，获得个人的慰藉（参见上文关于这种崇拜形式的印度教对应物达显）。因为只有在家人才“迷信”到从事这种为神学所贬斥的崇拜行为，所以赋予佛像生命的任务才交给在家画师。
en: The ceremony presents some interesting contrasts to the consecration of the Jagganath images, as well as many points of continuity. The Brahmin/Daita relationship is partially inverted in the ritual division of labour in the Sinhalese Buddhist consecration ceremonies. In Puri, it is the Daita who animates the image by putting ‘life-substance' into it, and the Brahmin priest who paints in the eyes; in Sri Lanka, on the other hand, it is the monk (abbot) who places the relic into the Buddha statue, and the lay craftsman who paints in its eyes. This is a precise reflection of the difference between the Buddha (a dead human being with morally supernatural characteristics) and the Hindu gods, who are non-human immortals. A Buddha statue celebrates the possibility of ‘a good death' and monks are semi-dead individuals who aspire to the ultimate gooddeath condition. Consequently it is only appropriate that the handling of Buddha relics, which are pieces of a dead body, should be assigned to monks, who are semi-dead themselves, and who of course always preside over funerals (but not births and marriages) in Buddhist countries like Sri Lanka (or Thailand; cf. Tambiah 1985). In a sense, then, what the relic does is make the Buddha statue like the Buddha, by making it ‘dead' through the insertion of a ‘death-substance'-in the rather paradoxical sense that Buddha-hood implies death-in-life. However, one can see that this ritual procedure hardly amounts to the ‘animation' of the image. Gombrich understands this as the means of ‘legitimating' the statue as a Buddha image, so that from the monkish perspective no taint of idolatry arises. For the laity things are otherwise. Buddha is really a god, and approaching the statue of the Buddha, the lay worshipper, immersed in life and sin, seeks personal reassurance through communion with the Buddha's living presence, conveyed through the eyes (see above on the Hindu equivalent of this form of worship, darshan). Because only lay people are ‘superstitious' enough to engage in such theologically decried acts of worship, it is the lay craftsman who is charged with the task of animating the Buddha image.

zh: 执行者认为这一仪式非常危险，周围环绕着禁忌。仪式由制作佛像的画师执行，此前要举行数小时的仪式，确保没有灾祸降临于他。这种灾祸是所有僧伽罗治疗仪式的对象，其概念化并不精确，但起因于仪式中的差错、触犯禁忌，或以其他方式引起某个超自然存在的恶意注意，后者通常以一瞥（balma，恶视）传达灾祸。画师在吉祥时刻点画眼睛，随后与同事单独留在关闭的神庙里，其余所有人连外门都远远避开。此外，画师不敢直视佛像的脸，而是背对着它，侧身或越过肩膀看着一面镜子作画，镜子承接了他正在赋予生命的神像的目光。画完的一刻，画师自己也带上了危险的目光。他被蒙着眼领出去，直到眼睛将要落在某物上的那一刻才除去遮盖，他随即用一剑象征性地毁掉那物。（Gombrich 1966: 24–5）［这可以是一头动物，比如公牛，但也可以用一只罐子或一棵流汁液的树替代。］
en: The ceremony is regarded by its performers as very dangerous and is surrounded with tabus. It is performed by the craftsman who made the statue, after several hours of ceremonies to ensure that no evil will come to him. This evil, which is the object of all Sinhalese healing rituals, is imprecisely conceptualised, but results from making mistakes in ritual, violating tabus, or otherwise arousing the malevolent attention of a supernatural being, who usually conveys the evil by a gaze (balma). The craftsman paints in the eyes at an auspicious moment and is left alone in the closed temple with only his colleagues, while everyone else stands clear even of the outer door. Moreover, the craftsman does not dare to look the statue in the face, but keeps his back to it and paints sideways or over his shoulder while looking into a mirror, which catches the gaze of the image he is bringing to life. As soon as the painting is done the craftsman himself has a dangerous gaze. He is led out blindfolded and the covering is only removed from his eyes when they will first fall upon something which he then symbolically destroys with a sword stroke. (Gombrich 1966: 24-5) [This could be an animal, such as a bull, but a pot, or a tree which exudes sap can be substituted.]

zh: 镜子的细节令人想起普里的婆罗门祭司用铜镜“沐浴”神像的做法——把水泼向它们的映像。但普里的婆罗门在点画眼睛时并不怕直视神像。与贾甘纳特的眼睛不同，佛陀的眼睛初次睁开时，会让为佛像开眼的人丧命（Artist-A ⟶ Artist-P 的一例；参见上文3.11节）。画师必须随即杀死某个生灵，自己才免于一死。这与佛教神学相去甚远；古时画师在执行仪式时要装扮成“国王”，也就是说，装扮成僧侣的反面——一个暴烈的、世俗的形象，通过自己牺牲宗教功德，让他人（僧侣、信众）得以获取功德。
en: The detail of the mirror recalls the use of bronze mirrors by the Brahmin priests of Puri to ‘bathe' the images by splashing water over their reflections. But the Puri Brahmins are unafraid to look at the images directly while painting in their eyes. Unlike the eyes of Jagganath, the eyes of the Buddha, when first opened, inflict death on the very person who performs the opening (a case of Artist-A ⟶ Artist-P; see above, Sect. 3.11). The craftsman must thereupon slay some creature in order not to die himself. This is very far from theologically Buddhist, and in olden times, the craftsman was dressed as a ‘king' while performing the ceremony, that is to say, as the negation of a monk, a violent, worldly figure, who by sacrificing religious merit himself, allows others (monks, devotees) to achieve it.

zh: 弗里德伯格（1989: 95）在其关于宗教形象及其他类型形象之接受的宏著中评论理查德·贡布里希时，提出了一个非常基本的问题：这类形象之所以（在宗教上）强大而有效力，是因为开光仪式赋予了它们重要的、隐秘的特质，还是因为它们首先是形象，借摹仿之力与它们所表现的神祇相连？他援引伽达默尔的支持，选择把再现放在首位。他论证说，形象之所以起作用，是因为它们具有内在的表意功能，这种功能可以与那类未经艺术塑形为人类、神祇等样貌的宗教物品（如舍利）所具有的效力区分开来。这种观点对艺术史家是必要的，无疑也是恰当的，因为他必须把“形象的力量”与纯然未成形之物的力量区分开来，无论后者的起源多么神圣、多么富于献祭意味。然而人类学家的处境略有不同。人类学家首要打交道的“与人相似的对象”，不是肖像、模拟像、偶像之类，而就是人本身。弗里德伯格对艺术摹仿之中心地位的强调，从人类学上说，必须置于这样的语境中：要“再现”一个人乃至一位神祇，最常见的承担者不是任何模拟像，而是扮演角色的人类行动者。教堂里可能塞满基督的形象，但基督教崇拜中基督的首要扮演由祭司承担，他扮演基督，在举行弥撒、诵念基督言辞时充当基督的形象。这并不是要驳回弗里德伯格的问题——下一节我还会回到它——但在离开开光这一话题之前，把我们考察过的两套开光仪式与第三个作比较是有趣的：在第三套仪式中，神性的“索引”根本不是雕刻的形象，而是一个人。
en: Freedberg (1989: 95), commenting on Richard Gombrich in his magnificent treatise on the reception of religious and other types of images, raises a very basic question. Are images such as these powerful and efficacious (religiously) because of the ceremonies of consecration which have endowed them with significant, occult, characteristics, or is it because they are, first and foremost, images, linked by the power of mimesis to the deities they represent? Citing the support of Gadamer, he opts to assign primacy to representation. He argues that images work because they have intrinsic signifying-functions, which can be separated from the kind of efficacy possessed by religious objects (such as relics) which have not been shaped and formed by art into the semblance of persons, deities, etc. Such a point of view is necessary, and no doubt proper, for the art historian, who has to distinguish the ‘power of images' from the power of mere unformed things, however sacred and sacrifying their origins. The anthropologist is in a slightly different position, however. The ‘objects which resemble human beings' with which the anthropologist deals, primarily, are not portraits, effigies, idols, and so forth, but simply human beings themselves. Freedberg's emphasis on the centrality of artistic mimesis has, anthropologically, to be set in the context in which the ‘representation' of a human being, or indeed a deity, is most commonly undertaken, not by any kind of effigy, but by a human actor playing a role. Churches may be stuffed with images of Christ, but the primary enactment of Christ in Christian worship is undertaken by the priest, who plays Christ and serves as Christ's image in performing the mass and uttering Christ's words. This is not to dismiss Freedberg's question, to which I will return in the next section, but before leaving the subject of consecration, it is interesting to compare the two consecration sequences we have examined, with a third, in which the ‘index' of the divinity is not a carved image at all, but a human being.

zh: 库玛丽普贾（Kumaripuja），即将年幼的处女奉为女神来崇拜（主要是杜尔迦的一种形态），在印度广泛流传，也是加德满都谷地尼瓦尔人宗教体系的一个特色，迈克尔·艾伦（1976）对这一崇拜做过细致研究。尼瓦尔地区约有九到十位活女神，其中最重要的是传统上与王室相联系的那一位。这位处女是凶猛的王室神塔莱珠的一种形态，塔莱珠本身又是杜尔迦的一种形态——印度教诸神中中那位暴烈而情色的女神，骑狮挥剑，斩杀了水牛魔。艾伦的分析集中于一个悖论：一个尚未初潮的处女如何竟能表现如此可怖的神祇；但我们关心的只是她神圣化的机制。
en: Kumaripuja, the worship of the goddess (primarily a form of Durga) in the form of a young virgin girl, is widely disseminated in India, and is a particular feature of the religious system of the Newars of the Kathmandu valley, where the cult has been the subject of a detailed study by Michael Allen (1976). There are some nine or ten living goddesses in the Newar region, of whom the most important is the one traditionally associated with the royal household. The virgin girl is a form of the fierce royal deity, Taleju, who herself is a form of Durga, the violent and erotic goddess in the Hindu pantheon, the slayer of the buffalodemon who rides on a lion and brandishes a sword. Allen's analysis concentrates on the paradox whereby a virgin, premenstrual girl comes to represent so fearsome a divinity, but what concerns us is only the mechanics of her divinization.

zh: 与此同时，处女崇拜可以与印度更常见的神灵（或恶魔）附体类型区分开来。那种形式的神灵附体是暂时的，通常是迷狂的；灵媒进入出神状态，成为神灵的“马”，以神灵的身份发声，并“玩耍”一阵（跳舞、荡秋千等；参见 Gell 1978）。库玛丽的情况没有任何迷狂出神的意味。这一身份是半永久的：一经祝圣（在两三岁时），库玛丽就是、并始终是女神本人，直到解除神圣身份的时刻——当某些“负面征兆”出现时，理论上是乳牙脱落，实际上是月经来潮。库玛丽出自一个特定种姓，他们是佛教徒，传统上依附于加德满都的寺院，这些寺院被现王朝解散。就种姓而言，她不造成污染，但又多少处于印度教等级体系之外。库玛丽的候选人必须到了会走会说的年龄，容貌无瑕，未落乳牙，等等。她的星象必须吉祥，尤其在与国王的关系方面。下面是艾伦对她就位情形的记述，发生在杜尔迦的节日德赛节（Dasain，即达萨拉）末尾：
en: Virgin-worship can, meanwhile, be distinguished from the more common type of divine (or demonic) possession which is found in India. Possession by the deity, in this form, is temporary and generally ecstatic; the medium goes into trance and becomes a ‘horse' for the deity, making utterances in the person of the deity, and ‘playing' for a while (dancing, swinging on a swing, etc.; cf. Gell 1978). There is no suggestion of ecstatic trance in the case of the kumari. This position is semi-permanent; once consecrated (at the age of 2 or 3), a kumari is and remains the goddess in person until the moment of deconsecration which transpires when certain ‘negative signs' arrive-loss of milk teeth in theory, in practice, menstruation. The kumari comes from a particular caste, who are Buddhists, traditionally attached to the monasteries of Kathmandu which were disbanded by the present royal dynasty. She is, in caste terms, nonpolluting but somewhat outside the Hindu hierarchical system. A candidate for kumari-hood must be old enough to walk and talk, of unblemished appearance, having lost no milk teeth, etc. Her horoscope must be auspicious, especially with regard to the king. Here is Allen's account of the circumstances of her installation, which occur at the end of Dasain (Dassara) the festival of Durga:

zh: 夜幕降临时，八头代表恶魔的水牛被割喉宰杀，血高高喷向供有塔莱珠神像的神龛。几小时后，约在午夜，又有54头水牛和54只山羊以同样的方式宰杀。不难想象，［塔莱珠神庙的］小庭院此时已血流成河……这时，通常在凌晨一点左右，被选中的小女孩被带到入口。她应当独自沿着抬高的边缘顺时针行走，直到抵达血迹斑斑的塔莱珠神龛。她必须走进去，始终保持着完全平静的神态；如果一切顺利，她就被带上楼，进一间小屋举行就位仪式……在例行的净化与其他预备仪式之后，主祭司主持核心仪式，从女孩身上除去她过去的一切经历，让塔莱珠之灵进入一个全然纯净的人体内。女孩赤身坐在祭司面前，祭司逐一净化她身体的敏感部位，一边诵念真言，一边用一小束草、树皮、树叶等纯净之物触碰每个部位。六个敏感部位是她的眼睛、喉咙、乳房、肚脐、阴道与外阴。随着他除去污秽，据说女神之灵进入女孩体内时，她的身体会渐渐发红。
en: At nightfall eight buffaloes representing the demon are killed by having their throats slit so that the blood jets high towards the shrine that contains the Taleju icon. A few hours later at about midnight a further 54 buffaloes and 54 goats are killed in a similar manner. As may well be imagined, the small courtyard [of the Taleju temple] is by then awash with blood ... At this point, usually about 1.00 A.M. the small Kumari-elect is brought to the entrance. She is supposed to walk by herself, in a clockwise direction around the raised edge until she reaches the bloody Taleju shrine. She must enter it, still maintaining a perfectly calm demeanour, and if all is well she is then taken upstairs to a small room for the installation ceremony ... after the usual purificatory and other preliminary rites, the chief priest performs the main ceremony in which he removes from the girl's body all of her previous life's experience so that the spirit of Taleju may enter a perfectly pure being. The girl sits naked in front of the priest while he purifies each of her sensitive body areas in turn by reciting a mantra and by touching each area with a small bundle of such pure things as grass, tree bark and leaves. The six sensitive parts are her eyes, throat, breasts, navel, vagina and vulva. As he removes the impurities the girl is said to steadily become redder and redder as the spirit of the goddess enters into her.

zh: 到这一步，女孩被穿上衣服，梳成库玛丽发式，点上红色提卡、第三只眼，戴上珠宝等等，然后坐上她雕工精美的木宝座，祭司已在座面上画好塔莱珠威力强大的室利扬特拉（sri yantra）曼荼罗。她还手持塔莱珠之剑，最终而完整的转变正是在此刻发生。值得注意的是，虽然从今往后直到数年后被取消资格，她将被一直视为库玛丽，但人们也相信，只有在盛装端坐宝座之时，她才完全成为库玛丽。其余时候，尤其是与朋友随意玩耍时，她一部分是自己，一部分是库玛丽。（Allen 1976: 306–7）
en: At this stage the girl is dressed and made up with Kumari hairstyle, red tika, third eye, jewellery, etc., and then sits on her beautifully carved wooden throne on the seat of which the priest has painted the powerful sri yantra mandala of Taleju. She also holds the sword of Taleju and it is at this point that the final and complete transformation takes place. It is worth noting that though from now until her disqualification some years later she will be continuously regarded as Kumari, it is also believed that it is only when fully made up and sitting on her throne that identification is complete. At other times, especially when casually playing with friends, she is partly herself and partly Kumari. (Allen 1976: 306-7)

zh: 在多大程度上，我们能看出库玛丽作为塔莱珠“活神像”的就位与更常规偶像的就位仪式之间的平行关系？与我们前面的每个例子一样，库玛丽的祝圣分两个阶段进行，一个聚焦于她的内部，一个聚焦于她的外部。第一阶段是从入选女孩体内“清空”她过去的人生（即她作为单纯人类的人格、能动性），这些具体体现为从她的孔口——眼睛、喉咙、外阴等——除去的污秽。她成为一只“中空的容器”，通过抽出全部原有内容，可以引入新的内容，即塔莱珠女神之灵。在我看来，这一阶段相当于贾甘纳特神像开光中代塔人在像内凿出腔穴、置入（外来的）生命物质的阶段。但正如艾伦明确指出的，完成这一步之后，转变仍未完成。
en: To what extent can one detect a parallelism between the installation of the kumari as a ‘living icon' of Taleju, and the installation rites of more conventional idols? As with each of our previous examples, the consecration of the kumari proceeds in two phases, one focusing on her interior and the other focusing on her exterior. The first phase consist of the ‘emptying' of the kumari-elect of her past life (i.e. her personhood, agency, as a mere human being), which is objectified as the impurities removed from her orifices, eyes, throat, vulva, etc. She becomes a ‘hollow vessel' into which, through the extraction of all previous contents, new contents may be drawn; that is, the spirit of the goddess Taleju. This phase, it seems to me, is the equivalent of the phase in the consecration of the Jagganath images in which the Daitas hollow out a cavity in the image and place therein a (foreign) life-substance. But after this has been effected, the transformation, as Allen makes clear, is still not complete.

zh: 祝圣的第二阶段是把库玛丽“包裹”在塔莱珠的衣饰中，为她施彩，并赋予女神的首要持物——她的剑。艾伦没有特别强调这一点，但库玛丽身份最醒目的视觉象征，其实是画在她额头中央的那只额外的“眼睛”——第三只眼。当然，祭司不必像对待木雕偶像那样为她点画瞳仁——她自有非常漂亮的眼睛。但他们用夸张的妆容勾勒她原有的眼睛，此外还在上方加画一只巨大的眼睛（见
）。为库玛丽画上一只额外的眼睛，与为常规偶像点画眼睛，两者之间的平行无疑相当醒目。更一般地说，穿衣、施彩、登座、授予兵器，显然对应我前面讨论过的“外部”赋灵策略。此外，库玛丽还以通常的方式从外部被赋予生命：诵念神圣言辞，以及坐于威力强大的魔法图纹室利扬特拉曼荼罗之上所产生的转喻效应。
en: The second phase of consecration consists of ‘wrapping' the kumari in the dress of Taleju, and painting her, as well as providing her with the goddess's primary attribute, her sword. Allen does not make much of the fact, but the most striking visual symbol of kumari-hood, is actually the extra ‘eye', the third eye, which is painted on the middle of her forehead. Of course, the priests do not have to paint in her pupils, as they would if she were a wooden idol-she has very pretty eyes of her own. But they outline her existing eyes with exaggerated make-up, besides adding an enormous painted eye above them (see

). The parallel between the making-up of the kumari with an extra eye and the painting-in of the eyes of conventional idols is surely rather striking. In more general terms it is clear that the dressing, painting, enthronement, and provision of weapons correspond to the ‘external' strategy of animation which I discussed earlier. Besides which, the kumari is externally animated in the usual way by the recitation of sacred words, and the metonymic effect of being seated on a magical design of great power, the sri yantra mandala.

zh: 简言之，库玛丽的祝圣与其他偶像的祝圣几乎没有分别，除了库玛丽会走、会说，神灵体现为一个活人，而非制成品。从本书勾勒的艺术人类学观点看，人工制品形式的“艺术品”与人之间界线并不分明：就它们可能在人类社会能动性网络中占据的位置而言，两者几乎完全可以等同看待。
en: In short, there is little to differentiate the consecration of the kumari from the consecration of any other idol, except that the kumari can walk, and talk, and is in fact incarnate as a human being rather than a manufactured artefact. From the point of view of the anthropology of art, as outlined in this work, there is an insensible transition between ‘works of art' in artefact form and human beings: in terms of the positions they may occupy in the networks of human social agency, they may be regarded as almost entirely equivalent.

zh: 7.13　结论：从个体到集体
en: 7.13　Conclusion: From the Individual to the Collective

zh: 至此，我结束这场关于偶像崇拜的长篇讨论。不过我承认，我所采取的特定路线始终把重心放在社会的、宗教的与心理的能动性上，而牺牲了审美的与艺术的能动性。弗里德伯格那个中肯的反驳仍然摆在我面前：沿这条路走得太远，就会看不到艺术的特殊性。我认为，就每一件单独的艺术品（索引）而言，人类学分析总是要以关系语境为重，也就是着眼于作品“周边”的施动者与受动者关系网，把艺术或审美形式放在次要位置；但当我们不是“单独地”而是作为艺术品的集合体来考虑艺术品时，情况就不同了。到目前为止，我分析的每一个索引都被视为嵌入特定社会语境的单一实体。然而，艺术品从来不只是单一实体；它们是艺术品类别的成员，其意义关键性地受到它们作为个体与同类别其他成员之间关系的影响，也受到这一类别与一个风格整体——一个文化上或历史上特定的艺术生产体系——之内其他艺术品类别之间关系的影响。
en: Thus I conclude this extended discussion of idolatry. I recognize, however, that the particular line I have taken has consistently resulted in the emphasis being placed on sociological, religious, and psychological agency at the expense of aesthetic and artistic agency. And I am left with Freedberg's pertinent objection: to travel too far down this road is to lose sight of art's specificity. While I hold that where each individual work of art (index) is concerned, anthropological analysis is always going to emphasize the relational context at the expense of artistic or aesthetic form, the network of agent patient relations ‘in the vicinity' of the work of art-the same does not apply when we come to consider artworks, not ‘individually' but as collectivities of artworks. So far, each index that I have subjected to analysis has been regarded as a singular entity, embedded in a particular social context. However, artworks are never just singular entities; they are members of categories of artworks, and their significance is crucially affected by the relations which exist between them, as individuals, and other members of the same category of artworks, and the relationships that exist between this category and other categories of artworks within a stylistic whole-a culturally or historically specific art-production system.

zh: 换言之，艺术品像人一样，也有家族、世系、部落和整个群体。它们彼此之间有关系，也与创作一件件作品并使它们得以流通的人有关系。可以说，它们联姻，生育带有祖先印记的后代。艺术品是作为集体现象的“文化”的显现，它们像人一样，受到文化的塑造。到目前为止，围绕艺术品的集体性问题都未加考虑。要开启这些问题，必须采用一套新的说法。在这里，我可以弥补写了这么多页、似乎偏离了通常理解的艺术品研究的缺憾。我将暂时搁置“索引”、能动性溯因之类的术语，回到更常规的词汇。因为有一个“常规的”艺术理论概念，即使最激进的艺术人类学家也无法置之不理——风格概念。风格是把艺术品联合成群体、成集合体的和谐原理，对应于人类学的“文化”主题。文化其实就是风格，正如费尔南德斯在一篇颇具影响力的论述中所提出的（1973）。
en: Artworks, in other words, come in families, lineages, tribes, whole populations, just like people. They have relations with one another as well as with the people who create and circulate them as individual objects. They marry, so to speak, and beget offspring which bear the stamp of their antecedents. Artworks are manifestations of ‘culture' as a collective phenomenon, they are, like people, enculturated beings. So far, none of the collective issues surrounding the work of art have been considered. In order to broach these issues, it is necessary to adopt a new register. Here, I can make amends for having written so many pages which may have seemed tangential to the study of works of art as normally understood. I shall, for a while, desist from the terminology of ‘indexes' and abductions of agency, and suchlike, reverting to a more conventional vocabulary. Because there is one ‘conventional' art-theoretical concept which even the most radical anthropologist of art cannot put to one side-the concept of style. Style, which is the harmonic principle which unites works of art into groups, into collectivities, corresponds to the anthropological theme of ‘culture'. Culture is style, really, just as Fernandez suggested in a deservedly influential discussion (1973).

zh: 每一件单独的艺术品都是某些风格原则的投射，这些原则构成更大的统一体；正如在亲属制社会中，每个个体都被视为继嗣、联姻与交换原则在此时此地的投射。风格概念使我们第一次能够专注于艺术品本身，讨论那些看起来确实属于其“审美”属性的东西。所以，让我向读者中的唯美主义者与艺术爱好者们保证（如果在我向他们倾泻了这么多辱骂之后还有剩的话）——你们已经翻到了本书中你们也许唯一会乐意读的一章。
en: Each individual work of art is the projection of certain stylistic principles which form larger unities, just as each individual, in a kin-based society, is regarded as a projection, into the here and now, of principles of descent and alliance and exchange. The concept of style allows us, for the first time, to concentrate exclusively on works of art as such, and to discuss what may appear, indeed, to be their ‘aesthetic' properties. So let me reassure those of my readers who are aesthetes and art-lovers (if I have any left after all the abuse I have showered on their heads)--you have reached the one chapter in this book you might possibly enjoy reading.

zh: 印本在本处及下一段重引的关系式中均少一闭方括号。英文照录，中文在“原型-A”后补齐，以显示层级。
en: A closing square bracket is missing here and in the formula in the following paragraph. The English follows the print edition, and the Chinese restores the bracket after ‘Prototype-A’.

zh: 在萨摩亚，织入构成酋长家族嫁妆的最名贵细席中的红羽，与处女陶普（taupou）的初夜之血相关联——她注定要传续酋长权力。
en: In Samoa the red feathers woven into the most prestigious fine mats forming chiefly dowries were associated with the hymeneal blood of the virgin taupou, the predestined reproducer of chiefly power.

zh: 与这种“捆缚”神的观念相关的，是古代常见的一种做法：用链条与镣铐把神庙中的神像拴住，以防它们逃走、把庇护转给敌对城邦（参见 Freedberg 1989: 74–5）。
en: Related to this idea of ‘binding’ the god is the practice, which was common in antiquity, of restraining the images of the gods in temples with chains and manacles, to prevent them from escaping and transferring their protection to rival cities (cf. Freedberg 1989: 74–5).

zh: 但参见维特科尔论文艺复兴建筑比例理论中的拟人要素，阿克曼论贝尼尼的广场，等等。
en: But cf. Wittkower on anthropomorphic elements in Renaissance theories of architectural proportion, Ackerman on Bernini’s piazza, etc.

zh: 然而奇怪的是，据民族志学者阿兰·巴巴赞说，当代鲁鲁图人对于他们知道曾在阿阿内部的神有一套完全不同的说法。按鲁鲁图长老的说法，阿阿由一位名叫阿迈特赖的英雄制成时，内部有三个神。阿迈特赖是在访问了一座城市之后制作阿阿的，那座城市不是别处，正是伦敦——阿阿如今的收藏地；他到达那里是为了娶到鲁鲁图国王的养女（她已许配给他的兄弟），他被派去完成一项骑士故事般的寻访任务。在伦敦，阿迈特赖遇到了智慧之神（后来成了基督徒的神，由传教士带到鲁鲁图），他以著名的阿阿的形式复制了这位神的形象。阿阿内部的神是三个源于伦敦的波利尼西亚神：鲁姆埃图阿奥雷，又名特阿图阿梅图阿，即圣父；奥拉罗伊特阿塔，又名特阿图阿塔迈蒂，即圣子；特阿图阿艾特罗阿，又名特阿图阿瓦鲁阿迈泰，即圣灵。换言之，阿阿是三位一体借以抵达鲁鲁图的圣幕，早在传教士到来之前，便由一位鲁鲁图英雄带到了岛上。阿阿在伦敦，但它以基督教信仰的形式在鲁鲁图依然存在。
en: Curiously though, contemporary Rurutans, according to the ethnographer Alain Babadzan have a quite different theory about the gods which, they know, were once inside the A’a. According to the Rurutan elders, there were three gods inside the A’a when it was made, by a Hero named Amaiterai. Amaiterai made the A’a after visiting a city none other than London, present resting-place of the A’a, which he reached in fulfilment of a species of knightly quest, imposed on him in order to win the hand of the adopted daughter of the King of Rurutu, who had been promised to his brother. In London Amaiterai encountered the God of Wisdom (who later was the God of the Christians, brought to Rurutu by the missionaries) whose image he replicated in the form of the famous A’a. The gods inside the A’a were three Polynesian gods originating in London: Room-etua-ore, alias Te Atua Metua, alias God the Father; Aura-roiteata, alias Te Atua tamaiti, alias God the Son; and Te Atua Aiteroa, alias Te Atua Varua Maita’i, alias God the Holy Spirit. In other words, the A’a is the Tabernacle in which the Trinity arrived on Rurutu, by the agency of a Rurutan hero, long before the missionaries themselves arrived. The A’a is in London, but it is present on Rurutu in the form of Christian belief.

zh: 这一特权令人想起塔希提托奥剥皮之后的“羽毛交换”（上文7.6节）。贾甘纳特的曼纳经由他的蜕余物、身体各部分以及朱塔（jutha，残余物）等传播开来。顺带一提，上文7.10节讨论的埃及例子也是如此。每次神像的衣服更新，换下的衣服都分给重要人物，用作包裹自己尸体的木乃伊裹布。在波利尼西亚与印度，神的布／羽蜕余物造福生者，而在埃及，它们造福身在来世的死者。
en: This prerogative recalls the ‘feather exchange’ following the decortication of the Tahitian to’o (7.6 above). The mana of Jagganath is disseminated via his exuviae, his body-parts, jutha (leavings) etc. Incidentally, the same is true in the Egyptian example discussed in 7.10 above. Every time the idols’ clothes were renewed, the discarded garments were distributed to important persons, to use to wrap their own corpses in as mummy-cloths. Whereas in Polynesia and India, the cloth/feather exuviae of the god went to benefit the living, in Egypt they benefited the dead in the afterlife.
